- **Now and Uses items are one textarea per section, not one input per item** ([inc/admin-forms/now-page.php](inc/admin-forms/now-page.php), [inc/admin-forms/uses-page.php](inc/admin-forms/uses-page.php)). The old card rendered a labelled input and ↑ ↓ ✕ controls for *every line of content* — on a dozen-item page, twelve inputs and thirty-six buttons to say twelve short sentences.

  It also modelled the data wrongly. The stored artifact has always been a **text document whose items are lines**; the nested repeatable was a tree pretending to be one. A textarea is the edit affordance the storage already implies: reorder by moving a line, delete by deleting it, add by pressing Return. Sections keep their cards and reorder controls, because sections genuinely are a list. `/uses` uses `name | note` per line — the exact shape the stored document writes, so the field shows what gets saved.

  The change is confined to a **boundary normalizer**: `sn_now_rows_to_text()` and `sn_uses_rows_to_text()` keep their array contract and their existing tests, and a test proves the textarea and the old per-item inputs produce a **byte-identical document**. Both input shapes are accepted, so a tab left open across the update still saves correctly instead of silently posting nothing.

### Fixed

- **The same-site referer signal is withdrawn** ([inc/redirects-404-log.php](inc/redirects-404-log.php)). v10.47.0 promoted any 404 arriving with a referer from this site, reasoning that a real page pointing at a dead path is worth fixing. Driving it on live disproved that in one screen: **20 of the 26 "actionable" rows had been promoted by referer, and every one was machine noise** — `/phpinfo`, `/_profiler/phpinfo`, `/*`, and real site paths with a random 19-digit suffix bolted on (`/comments/3135222639369717147`).

  The error is worth naming precisely, because the v10.47.0 comment came close enough to be misleading. It said an *off-site* referer is attacker-controlled and must not count — true — and then missed that the header is **client-controlled whatever host it names**. Worse: a crawler walking this site sends a same-site referer *by definition*, so the rule promoted everything a bot happened to touch. Similarity alone had already found every genuine broken link in the same sample (`/provenance/verify` → `/verify`, `/es/about`, `/contact-us`), so the signal contributed noise and nothing else.

- **Two probe shapes that reach the log with no file extension to catch them** — `phpinfo` and `/_profiler` (the Symfony debug toolbar) join the probe substrings.

- **Crawler fuzzing: a real path with a long random number appended.** A path *segment* that is a bare run of 12+ digits is now filtered. The floor is 12 so ordinary numbers in a URL are untouched — `/notes/page/2`, `/2026/08/…` and `/notes/top-10-tools` are all pinned as still-captured.

> **Why PATCH:** narrows an over-eager classifier shipped in v10.47.0. No new capability, no schema change, no stored entry deleted — the withdrawn signal only ever affected which side of the split a row displayed on.

### Verification

`tests/redirects-404-log.php` **121 passed / 0 failed**, written from the exact paths the live screen promoted in error and watched red on all seven. Full sweep green; phpcs clean, falsified first.

## [10.47.0] - 2026-08-05

**Headline:** the 404 log stops asking you to make editorial decisions about scanner traffic — and stops letting that traffic evict your real broken links. Tools becomes Integrity.

### Fixed

- **The 404 log was lossy, not just noisy** ([inc/redirects-404-log.php](inc/redirects-404-log.php)). A live audit found all 200 slots occupied and roughly 95% of them automated probes: `/server.key`, `/id_rsa`, `/actuator/heapdump`, `/@fs/proc/self/environ`, `/filezilla.xml`. The cap is a FIFO, so a single scanner sweep — hundreds of distinct paths in minutes — pushed genuinely broken links out of the log **before they were ever seen**. The feature was quietly discarding the only entries it exists to surface.

  Three changes, in increasing order of importance:

  1. **The blocklist was widened** to the families it had no rule for — key and certificate material (`.key`, `.pem`, `.crt`…), archives, heap and log dumps, extensionless credential filenames (`id_rsa`, `known_hosts`, `.pgpass`), FTP client credential stores, traversal markers, and framework/appliance endpoints. It also gained `wp-config`, which it had somehow never had while filtering `wp-login` and `wp-admin`.
  2. **Eviction now prefers probes.** `sn_404_log_evict()` fills the cap with actionable entries first, so noise can never again displace signal.
  3. **A structural classifier, because a blocklist is always one campaign behind.** `sn_404_is_actionable()` inverts the question from "does this look hostile" to "could a redirect for this even make sense": a path qualifies when it resembles something published here — computed by the **existing** v9.81.0 levenshtein suggester, not a second heuristic to keep in sync — or when something on this site links to it. An off-site referer deliberately does not qualify; referers are attacker-controlled, and honouring them would hand any scanner a way to promote itself back into view.

- **The Redirects rail rendered every logged path as its own decision card** ([inc/redirects-admin.php](inc/redirects-admin.php)) — 200 cards, each politely offering to create a redirect for `/server.key`, all under an "Attention" pill. Actionable paths keep their cards; everything else collapses to one line with a count, a peek at the paths, and a single **Dismiss all probes** action that keeps genuinely broken paths. The probe line carries no attention pill: it is weather, not a task. Nothing is deleted on read.

- **Two duplicated sentences on the AI budget field** ([inc/admin-forms/ai-settings.php](inc/admin-forms/ai-settings.php)). With no cap set it said "AI features never pause on cost" and then, immediately, "Set 0 for no limit. When a cap is reached, AI features pause…". Introduced in v10.46.0.

- **Three leaves rendered as a narrow card in a wide tab.** `wide` only swaps the *wrapper* for a bare `.sn-section`; the card's own 820px cap survives it. Live, the AI, Pattern Adoption and Block Migrations leaves each drew a ~620px box with two thirds of the tab empty. The AI form now joins the Phase-4a field grid that Front-End and Identity already use — a short form earns its width by making the **fields** the columns — and the scanner cards uncap.

### New

- **Tools becomes Integrity, with a leaf that gives it a concept** ([inc/integrity-trust-admin.php](inc/integrity-trust-admin.php)). v10.46.0 emptied the junk drawer but left two leaves with no sentence covering both. Four of the eighteen health checks were never about content — the provenance triangle, the public ledger's own CI, the live rights signals, and whether those signals are still being anchored — yet they were reachable only as four rows interleaved with missing alt text, on a different tab from the console they are checking.

  The leaf **runs nothing and fetches nothing**: every number is read from the health scan that already ran, so opening it costs one option read, and the scan age is stated rather than hidden. A check missing from the scan renders as "not run", never as blank — a gap in a trust surface must not look like a pass.

### Changed

- **Leaf order within two tabs.** Measurement now reads Analytics → RSS → Machine Readers → Insights → Health: what was recorded, then what interprets it (`snt_mr_admin_register()` inserts rather than appends). AI reads Models & Budget → MCP Clients → Copilot Usage: both configuration leaves before the observation one, where it previously alternated.

> **Why MINOR:** a new user-visible surface (the Trust checks leaf) plus a new bulk action. No settings-schema change; the 404 log's stored shape is untouched and no entry is deleted on read.

### Verification

Full sweep **14,510 passed / 0 failed** (14,450 before; +60). phpcs clean, falsified first. The 404 spec was written from paths pulled off the live log and watched go red — 18 real probe shapes the shipped filter waved through.

## [10.46.0] - 2026-08-05

**Headline:** the settings page is regrouped by intent instead of by history — eight tabs, AI promoted out of a render-knobs form, the three content scanners reunited, and the collector endpoint moved to the screen that is actually about it.

### Changed

- **Eight top tabs, regrouped by what things ARE** ([inc/admin-tabs-data.php](inc/admin-tabs-data.php)). Eleven leaves had landed since the v6.18.0 IA was designed, each wherever there happened to be room. **Site** absorbs Front-End, Performance and Redirects — how the site behaves, as opposed to what is published on it — and is relabelled from `Identity & SEO`, the single leaf whose name it had been wearing. **Content** keeps the page editors. **Connections** gains Music, relabelled `Discography`, because what that leaf actually holds is a Spotify credential form. **Monitoring** becomes **Measurement** and gains RSS: the RSS leaf is feed-request analytics, and the old tab declared itself "observability-only" in the same file that called its first leaf a "SETTINGS-ONLY sub-tab" — all four of its leaves carry writes, so it is now named for what it holds rather than for a rule it never kept. **Tools** stops being a junk drawer whose own subtitle named three of its five leaves.

  **Labels changed; keys did not.** `tab=monitoring&sub=health` is hardcoded in five call sites, and every one of them still resolves. Every leaf that changed parent tab has an entry in `sn_admin_subtab_moves()`, which feeds both the GET 301 and the POST PRG — so old bookmarks and in-flight saves land in the same place.

### New

- **An AI tab** ([inc/admin-forms/ai-settings.php](inc/admin-forms/ai-settings.php)). A hard cap on monthly AI spend was field 10 of Content → Front-End, a form whose own intro described its contents as *"render knobs the companion theme reads via filters"*. The rest of the AI surface was scattered across four more tabs. The tab gathers the three settings that are configuration — prose model, vision model, monthly budget — with Copilot Usage and MCP Clients. The budget field now carries the spend-against-cap meter the analytics settings hub already had, reusing that component rather than growing a second one.

  The three settings **keep the `theme.` key namespace**; renaming them would need a migration and would break the readers in `analytics-render-settings.php` and `ai-bootstrap.php`. Where a value is edited and where it is stored are separate questions, and only the first one moved.

- **Pattern Adoption is its own leaf** ([inc/pattern-adoption-admin.php](inc/pattern-adoption-admin.php)), beside Tags and Block Migrations — three sibling content scanners that had been sitting in three different tabs, one of which ([inc/block-migrations-admin.php](inc/block-migrations-admin.php)) already documented itself as *"Mirrors inc/pattern-adoption-admin.php structurally."*

  It also **loses a gate it never had a reason for.** The card rendered inside the Health tab's action row behind `if ( $last_scan && … )`, where `$last_scan` is a *health* scan. Pattern adoption has its own scan and its own transient and needs nothing from the health one; the precondition was an artifact of where the card sat. Anyone who had not run a health scan could not discover the feature at all, and nothing explained why.

### Fixed

- **The collector endpoint was configured under Content → RSS** ([inc/analytics-render-settings.php](inc/analytics-render-settings.php)). Every first-party beacon on the site posts to that URL; its own helper text called it *"the Cloudflare Worker's `/_sn/px` route"*, on a leaf about feed subscribers. It moves to Measurement → Analytics, next to the credentials that read what it collects and the worker-version card that probes the same origin — and the read-only "Collector URL" row disappears from that leaf's own *"Configured elsewhere"* block, which had been mirroring the pipeline's own ingest endpoint as though it belonged to someone else.

  **The half that is easy to miss:** the RSS save branch rebuilds its whole settings array from `$_POST` and fell back to `$defaults` for any absent key. With the field gone from that form, every RSS save would have silently reset a customised collector back to `home_url('/_sn/px')`. It now falls back to the **stored** value, and the new writer merges a single key instead of replacing the array. Both halves are pinned by [tests/rss-collector-move.php](tests/rss-collector-move.php).

- **Two moved leaves would have shipped with dead Suggest buttons** ([inc/admin-menu.php](inc/admin-menu.php)). The `health-suggest-actions.js` enqueue guard was a pair of hardcoded tab/sub comparisons, and Pattern Adoption and Block Migrations both changed address in this release. Not hypothetical: the same guard shape caused v6.47.2, where the v6.x IA moved Health under Monitoring, the stale `'health' === $_GET['tab']` check stopped matching, and *every* Suggest button was dead on every site — with no console error and no failing test. The leaf list is now data (`sn_admin_suggest_js_leaves()`), and [tests/admin-menu.php](tests/admin-menu.php) asserts each entry both resolves against the live registry and actually enqueues at that address, so the next move fails a suite instead of failing silently.

- **Block Migrations was drawing a card inside a card.** Its render function has always emitted its own `.sn-fieldset`, but the leaf was not marked `wide`, so the dispatcher wrapped that card in a second one. Invisible while it sat alone in Tools; obvious the moment it stood next to its two siblings.

- **The Health tab's action row is gone with it.** That two-up grid existed to pair Run scan with the Opportunities card so neither sat capped beside a dead column. With one child left, `auto-fit` would have stretched a short form edge to edge — the bare-stretched lone form the Phase-4b width rule forbids. Wrapper and its now-dead CSS both removed.

- **Stale tab paths across 15 files and 4 docs** — the same drift class the v10.45.1 docblock sweep addressed, refreshed for the tabs this release moved.

> **Why MINOR:** new user-visible surfaces (the AI tab, the Pattern Adoption leaf) and a reorganized one. No settings-schema change — every stored key keeps its name — and every moved leaf keeps working through the existing redirect resolver, so nothing requires user action.

### Verification

Full sweep **14,450 passed / 0 failed** (14,367 before this release; +83 assertions). phpcs clean, falsified first with an `echo $_GET['x']` probe confirming `WordPress.Security.EscapeOutput` fires. The target IA was written into `tests/admin-registry.php` and `tests/admin-ia-redirect.php` **first** and watched go red before the registry was touched.

## [10.45.1] - 2026-08-05

**Headline:** three independent admin fixes surfaced by the IA audit — a desktop icon that opened the wrong page, two unreachable symbols, and four docblocks pointing at tabs retired four majors ago.

### Fixed

- **The Machine Readers desktop icon opened the SN Dashboard** ([inc/desktop-mode-integration.php](inc/desktop-mode-integration.php)). It passed `'sn-theme-options&tab=monitoring&sub=machine-readers'` — a full query string — to `snt_desktop_admin_url()`, which expects a bare page slug. No slug matched, so the resolver fell through to its `'dashboard'` default: a link that loads perfectly and goes to the wrong place, the exact failure mode the `sn-analytics` special case beside it was written to prevent. The helper now takes an optional explicit `$sub`, and the caller passes `('sn-monitoring', 'machine-readers')`.
- **Two unreachable release-notes symbols removed** ([inc/admin-post-actions.php](inc/admin-post-actions.php), [inc/admin-flash-messages.php](inc/admin-flash-messages.php)). `sn_handle_release_notes_draft()` was absent from `sn_admin_post_handlers()`, so nothing could dispatch it, and its `release_notes_failed` flash could never fire. The leaf went out in v10.0.0.
- **Four docblocks naming retired tabs** — `admin-forms/front-end.php` said "Tools tab" (moved to Content in v6.18.0), `admin-forms/indexnow.php` said "Automation" (retired v6.18.0), `edge-admin.php` claimed it renders inside Monitoring → Analytics (it renders in the WP Dashboard → Analytics dashboard), and `audit-log-admin.php` quoted an if/elseif dispatch arm the registry replaced in v6.17.x. Not cosmetic: the precedent is the Reading Time cleanup UI, which pointed at a slug retired in v6.18.0 and *"had been broken for versions"* before anyone noticed.

> **Why PATCH:** one user-visible link fix plus dead-code and comment removal. No new capability, no API change, no settings touched.

### Verification

Full sweep **14,367 passed / 0 failed**; phpcs clean and falsified. The larger IA reorganization these were found alongside is scaffolded, not shipped — see `docs/superpowers/audits/2026-08-05-admin-ia-audit.md`.

## [10.45.0] - 2026-08-04

**Headline:** the CMS page seeds are re-frozen from the live post-migration state, so a fresh install now reproduces the current design instead of landing on a hero the migration chain could never reach.

### Fixed

- **Three of the four CMS page seeds could not enter the split-hero migration chain** ([inc/seed-content/](inc/seed-content/)). `sn_split_hero_targets()` gates each swap on an md5 of the page's *live* hero band frozen 2026-08-03. The `about`, `services` and `music` seeds hashed differently, so the one-shot permanently skipped them and a fresh install kept a hero that was neither the old live one nor the current split one — still carrying the superseded `clamp(3rem, 7vw, 5.5rem)` title and 1400px bands below the hero, plus (on `services`) the credibility strip removed by owner decision in v10.37.5.
- **`contact` was the opposite problem, and the more interesting one.** Its seed *did* match the entry hash, so the chain fired — but the live page has since moved through four further revisions to `split-hero-contact-hero-v5`, which the v1 seed knows nothing about. A fresh install would have replayed the entire chain to arrive where live already is.

  All four seeds are now re-frozen **from the live bodies themselves**, which is the only authoritative source: for `about`, `services` and `music` the live hero band was verified **byte-identical** to the corresponding `split-hero-*.html`, and for `contact` it matched `split-hero-contact-hero-v5.html` — proving the endpoint rather than assuming it.

### Changed

- **`music-above.html` was re-frozen surgically, not wholesale** — only its leading hero band was swapped, plus one `1400px` → `1320px` fix. It is the *opening half* of a merge (`above` + existing page content + `below`), so copying the whole live body would have duplicated the Spotify-embeds wrapper and the discography section.

### Deliberately unchanged

- **The frozen hashes in `sn_split_hero_targets()`.** They describe the pre-split hero as it exists on an un-migrated install, so they remain the correct entry gate for one. Only a docblock note was added recording why they must stay.
- **The one-shot chain itself.** It is now a no-op for fresh installs (the seeds start at its endpoint) but is still the migration path for any install that has not run it.

### Verification

Every claim here was checked rather than assumed:

- Each re-frozen seed's leading band is **byte-identical to the live page's** leading band.
- Zero `1400px`, zero `sn-credibility-strip`, zero `clamp(3rem, 7vw, 5.5rem)` remain in any of the four.
- No `wp-image-*` classes and no `"id":` attachment references were introduced, so a fresh install references no media that would not exist.
- `music-above.html`'s block-comment imbalance is **pre-existing and unchanged** (`+1` open before and after) and balances against `music-below.html` — it is a split file by design.
- The `Catalog · Discography` idempotence sentinel that `sn_migrate_music_body()` tests for survives the band swap, in the exact raw-middot form the code matches.
- **The chain cannot carry a fresh install past the endpoint:** each migration maps every prior variant forward to the newest, and the newest appears only ever as an *output*, never as an input.
- Full sweep **14,367 passed / 0 failed** — identical to the pre-change count, so nothing pinning seed content regressed. phpcs clean.

> **Why MINOR:** seed content that determines what a fresh install renders is user-visible. No public API touched, no settings-schema change, no operator action required — and by construction this changes nothing on an existing install, where the seeds are read only by one-shots whose flags are long since set.

## [10.44.0] - 2026-08-04

**Headline:** the least-monitored coupling in the system gets enforced where it breaks — at the write boundary, not on a 24-hour poll — and the Machine Readers surface stops measuring the wrong thing.

### New

- **A structural contract for engine-generated page bodies, enforced at the write boundary** ([inc/generated-page-contract.php](inc/generated-page-contract.php)). `/resume`, `/now` and `/uses` are built by sync engines and stored as `post_content`. The suite pinned what the engines **build**; nothing pinned what is **stored** — and every failure in that coupling happened in the gap, each caught only by an owner screenshot: v10.33.1 (the `/resume` body shipped wrapped in `wp:html`, so WordPress enqueued no core block styles and the page rendered unstyled) and v10.33.3 (a band at a superseded width). The three upsert functions now refuse a body that has lost its structure, log it, and fire `snt_generated_page_write_refused`.
  - **This started as a 19th health check and that was the wrong shape.** The other 18 checks watch *ambient* drift — external links rot, edge headers change, the ledger CI goes red — things the world changes underneath us, where polling is the only option. Generated page bodies are not ambient: they change for exactly one reason, a write, which is an event observable at the moment it happens. Polling up to 24h later for something catchable at source is strictly weaker, and a 19th entry on a list already read as a single "18/18 passed" glance spends attention the other checks need. **The check count stays at 18.**
  - **Fail-closed, and cheap to be so.** An engine emitting markup that loses the layout is a bug, never a valid state, so refusing costs nothing real and leaves the previously-correct body in place — the page keeps rendering while the error names what was attempted.
  - **Deliberate asymmetry:** `/now` and `/uses` *are* `wp:html` by design (their builders wrap a raw `<div>`); `/resume` must be real block markup. The `wp:html` rule is asserted for `/resume` only, because a `wp:html` `/resume` **is** the v10.33.1 regression.
  - **Scope stated honestly:** this guards *engine* writes. It does **not** address v10.33.2 (an unchanged save skipped the sync) — nothing was written there, so a write guard has nothing to catch; that belongs to the sync path's own idempotence. Manual edits through the block editor are deliberately not blocked, because refusing an owner's own save would be hostile.

### Fixed

- **The rights-signals check never looked at the REST `Content-Signal` header** ([inc/health-check-rights-signals.php](inc/health-check-rights-signals.php)). v10.34.0 added `Content-Signal` to every REST response specifically to close a rights-surface gap, but the check whose entire job is that surface only read `robots.txt`. The header could vanish (regression, edge stripping, a `wp-config` override) with nothing going red. It now rides the same fail-closed rule as the robots.txt line and `TDM-Reservation`: presence alone is never enough, because `ai-train=yes` is the semantic **inverse** of the reservation rather than a weaker form of it.

### Changed

- **Machine Readers stops framing a healthy zero as a shortfall** ([assets/desktop-mode-widget-machine-readers.js](assets/desktop-mode-widget-machine-readers.js), [inc/machine-readers-admin.php](inc/machine-readers-admin.php)). The widget row read "…of the rights files", and the tab copy asked "whether declared AI-training crawlers actually read the rights declarations that apply to them" — both implying the rights only reach a crawler that goes and fetches them. Since rights-signals worker **v1.5.0** the reservation (`TDM-Reservation`, `Content-Signal`, `Link rel=license`) rides **every** response, so a crawler receives it without ever touching the rights files. The row is now "…fetched rights files directly".
  - **The metric is kept, not deleted.** A non-zero value is a genuinely useful positive signal — a crawler that went looking for the declarations on purpose is doing compliance-checking. It simply stopped being a coverage measure, so the label stopped implying one.

### Docs

- **Ability and check counts recomputed from source, not edited by hand.** `docs/ai-abilities-catalog.md` claimed 65 abilities (50 plugin + 15 theme); the real figures are **81 (66 plugin + 15 theme)**. Door counts said 25 read / 35 read-write; actually **37 / 36** — and the doors overlap by design, so they were never meant to sum to the ability count. `README.md` said a 13-check scan (now 19) and 52 abilities with 25/35 doors.
- **15 abilities were registered but never tabled**, so the catalog under-reported the plugin surface by 15: the `sn-*` consolidated family (`sn-apply`, `sn-posts`, `sn-scan`, `sn-site-facts`, `sn-validate`) plus `cadence-flags`, `duplicate-body-scan`, `get-machine-readers-summary`, `get-post-content`, `keyword-candidates`, `link-candidates`, `list-posts`, `near-duplicate-scan`, `topic-clusters`, and `update-post-surfaces`. All now listed with their source files.
- **`draft-release-notes` removed from the catalog** — it was deleted in v10.0.0 but stayed documented as live.

> **Why MINOR:** a new enforced contract plus a new action hook (`snt_generated_page_write_refused`) is new user-visible capability. No removed or renamed public API, no settings-schema change, nothing requiring operator action.

### Verification

- Full sweep **14,361 passed / 0 failed**; phpcs clean and falsified first (injected `echo $_GET['x']`, confirmed `WordPress.Security.EscapeOutput` fires).

### Known, reported but not changed here

- **Three of the four CMS page seeds cannot enter the split-hero migration chain.** `sn_split_hero_targets()` keys on an md5 of each page's *live* hero band frozen 2026-08-03; the `about`, `services` and `music` seeds hash differently, so the one-shot permanently skips them on a fresh install (only `contact` matches). Their seed hero bands are a third variant — neither the old live hero nor the current split hero — and still carry the superseded `clamp(3rem, 7vw, 5.5rem)` title and 1400px bands below the hero. This only affects seeding a brand-new site, and fixing it means re-freezing page content rather than changing code, so it is left for a deliberate content pass. Note the earlier audit framing was wrong in its specifics: `music-above.html` is a **template part**, not a page body.

## [10.43.1] - 2026-08-04

### Fixed

- **The Desktop Mode "View on WordPress.org" button hider was dead code, twice over — the honest fix is removal, not a third selector** ([inc/desktop-mode-integration.php](inc/desktop-mode-integration.php)). *(This entry stays folded into 10.43.1, the version the previous cut already shipped under — same pattern as v10.42.0's REJECT #10: the review round is folded into the entry that hasn't tagged yet, not a new version.)* The original bullet in this same entry re-selectored an inline DOM patch (`admin_print_footer_scripts`, since v2.1.7) from a dead `a[href*="wordpress.org/plugins/…"]` selector to `wpd-button, os-button` — still targeting the button's real custom-element tag names, confirmed against `WordPress/openstation` tag `v0.9.8` and post-#475 trunk. **Adversarial review REJECTed that cut (REJECT #12)**: the new selector was exactly as dead as the old one, for a reason neither the original bug nor the first fix accounted for. The Installed-view detail panel — the button AND the plugin-Name table cell — renders inside an **open shadow root** (`attachShadow({mode:'open'})`, `WordPress/openstation src/ui/core/component.ts:88`; the panel is appended into a shadow `<tbody>` by `wpd-table.ts:1404-1433`, confirmed against upstream's own `installed-detail.ts:63-69`, which documents that document-level DOM access does not pierce this boundary). `document.body.querySelectorAll(...)` cannot traverse into shadow content regardless of what tag or class it queries for, and the `MutationObserver` this patch attached to `document.body` never observes mutations that happen *inside* a shadow root either — so no amount of re-selectoring, on either half of the patch, could ever have worked.

  **Misattributed-evidence resolution**: the patch's OWN docblock had called the DOM Name-decode half "belt and suspenders", implying `rest_prepare_plugin` (the wire-level filter, unchanged since v2.1.6/v2.1.7) was the primary fix and the DOM half a defensive backup. Investigation confirmed that framing was actually correct, just never verified: the DOM half chased the exact same shadow-rooted table as the button, so it was equally unreachable and had never been the working fix. `rest_prepare_plugin` — which edits the REST payload on the wire, before Desktop Mode ever renders into the shadow root, so there is nothing left for a DOM patch to defend — always was. It had zero test coverage anywhere in the repo until this round.

  **Fix — Option B, honest removal**: the entire `admin_print_footer_scripts` hook (both selector halves, the Name-decode half, the `MutationObserver`) is deleted, replaced with a docblock explaining why no document-scoped patch can ever reach this content and what real removal would require (a shadow-root hop at every custom-element boundary, a `MutationObserver` per shadow root rather than one at `document.body`, and label-matching re-scoped to only this plugin's own panel — a bare "WordPress.org" label match would otherwise hide the button for every *other* listed wp.org-hosted plugin too, per `installed-detail.ts:333`). With the button-hider half gone, `patch()` had no reachable target left in this codebase, so it is removed wholesale rather than kept running against text nodes it can never see. The 404 itself remains accepted as cosmetic — upstream's own fallback behavior for a self-hosted, non-wp.org-listed plugin, unreachable to fix from our side — and is now tracked upstream at [WordPress/openstation#492](https://github.com/WordPress/openstation/issues/492) rather than left as folklore in a code comment. `rest_prepare_plugin` (Name/Author decode, unconditional icon-url override) is untouched and remains the entire surviving fix for this surface.

  ([tests/desktop-mode-integration.php](tests/desktop-mode-integration.php) — the 11 assertions pinning the now-deleted `wpd-button`/`os-button` selector are replaced with 11 absence pins (both dead selectors, the label match, the idempotency marker, the `MutationObserver`, both DOM Name-decode constants and its match-and-replace) run against the source file directly, so a re-add anywhere in the file — not just inside the removed hook — still fails them; watched RED against `f2faa4b` first, 9 of the 11 failed exactly as predicted (2 were already true pre-round and stayed green as positive controls). `rest_prepare_plugin` gains real coverage for the first time: basename scoping (an out-of-scope plugin's Name is left untouched and never even written back), Name/Author decode, the unconditional icon-url override even when upstream had already populated the field, and — via a `set_data_calls` counter added to the `WP_REST_Response` test stub — proof the dirty-flag actually skips the write when nothing changed, not just that the final data happens to look right.) Full sweep: 378 files, 12,449 assertions, 0 failures. `php -l` clean on both touched files. PHPStan (315 files) clean. PHPCS clean.

## [10.43.0] - 2026-08-04

### Added

- **OpenStation rename compatibility layer** ([inc/openstation-compat.php](inc/openstation-compat.php), [docs/openstation-compat.md](docs/openstation-compat.md)). WordPress/openstation PR #475 (merged 2026-08-03, in trunk, **not yet in any tagged release** — the owner runs pre-rename Desktop Mode v0.9.8 today) renames the plugin from "Desktop Mode" to "OpenStation": `desktop_mode_*()` functions and hooks → `openstation_*()`, `DESKTOP_MODE_*` constants → `OPENSTATION_*`, `Desktop_Mode_*` classes → `Open_Station_*`, JS `wp.desktop` → `wp.os`, `window.desktopModeWidgets` → `window.openStationWidgets`, CSS `.desktop-mode-*` → `.os-*`. **The naming is `openstation_*`, not the mechanically-guessed `open_station_*`** — verified against real post-#475 source (no underscore between "open" and "station" anywhere: functions, hooks, or constants), and **there is no back-compat shim** (a fresh grep of post-#475 source for any `desktop_mode_*` name returns zero hits), so exactly one naming family is ever active per install. Every one of the 9 upstream hooks this plugin consumes (`dock_items`, `dock_placement`, `ai_tools`, `ai_system_prompt_appendix`, `ai_tool_called`, `agent_completed`, `agent_tool_result`, `living_tree_traffic`, `plugins_window_icon_url`) plus the JS widget-mount global, the `wp.desktop`/`wp.os` namespace, and the `desktop-mode.drop.files-detected`/`os.drop.files-detected` file-drop filter were **individually verified against real post-#475 source** (file:line, not derived from the rename table) — see docs/openstation-compat.md for the full audit trail. **Dual registration**: a single helper (`snt_os_compat_add_filter()`/`snt_os_compat_add_action()`) attaches every consumed hook's callback under both the pre-rename and post-#475 names, so the plugin works unchanged on either release line without version-branching every call site; the direct function CALLS this plugin makes into upstream (`register_command`/`register_widget`/`register_icon`/`is_enabled`/`ai_ability_tool_name` — no back-compat alias exists for these either) route through dispatch wrappers that prefer the post-#475 name when both exist, falling back to the pre-rename name. **Double-fire guards**: idempotent filters (schema normalizer, dock items/placement, icon URL, living-tree traffic) dual-register with no guard — computing the same pure transform twice is harmless — but handlers with real side effects (`ai_tool_called`'s option-counter increment, both agent-telemetry DB-insert seams) each guard against a hypothetical future transition shim firing both names for the same event, via a per-request identity hash (`snt_os_compat_seen_once()`); the system-prompt appendix filter gets a content-marker guard instead of a once-per-request flag, since the real callsite legitimately fires it twice per ordinary request (primary run + composed-reply leg) and a flag would wrongly suppress the second legitimate call. **JS**: a new `assets/desktop-mode-os-compat.js` prelude aliases `window.desktopModeWidgets`↔`window.openStationWidgets` and `window.wp.desktop`↔`window.wp.os` onto the same object before any widget script or `desktop-mode.js` runs (wired as an explicit dependency of every `sn-desktop-mode*` script handle) — zero edits to the 65 existing `wp.desktop`/`desktopModeWidgets` call sites across 9 widget files; `assets/desktop-dropzone.js`'s file-drop filter registers under both `desktop-mode.drop.files-detected` and `os.drop.files-detected`, with a `WeakSet` guarding against a hypothetical double-draft. **Behavior on pre-rename v0.9.8 is unchanged** — every existing test passes unmodified except two structurally-forced pin updates (a `function_exists()` string-match became a helper-function-name match, same underlying gate); **post-rename support is source-verified but not yet release-testable** — no post-#475 OpenStation release exists to test end-to-end against. RED-verified: the double-fire guards were confirmed to actually catch a simulated same-event double-fire (temporarily removed, tests failed exactly on the double-fire assertions, restored, green again). ([inc/openstation-compat.php](inc/openstation-compat.php), [assets/desktop-mode-os-compat.js](assets/desktop-mode-os-compat.js), [tests/openstation-compat.php](tests/openstation-compat.php) 40 asserts + new dual-registration/guard coverage across [tests/desktop-mode-integration.php](tests/desktop-mode-integration.php), [tests/ai-tool-invocation-log.php](tests/ai-tool-invocation-log.php), [tests/mcp-telemetry-agents.php](tests/mcp-telemetry-agents.php).)

**Adversarial review REJECTed the initial ship** (REJECT #11) on one HIGH and one MEDIUM plus three LOWs, all fixed in-worktree, watched-RED first for every behavioral change. **HIGH**: the double-fire guard (`snt_os_compat_seen_once()`) was a plain per-request boolean keyed on the call's full identity hash — it suppressed the SECOND of ANY two calls sharing that key, including two genuinely distinct, LEGITIMATE events that merely hash identically within one PHP process. Not hypothetical: `openstation_agent_tool_result` (real post-#475 `runner.php:579`) carries no `call_id`, so two identical tool calls with byte-identical output within one agent run are indistinguishable by payload, and a Copilot `$request_id` is per-RUN (`search.php:888-890`, reused across the iteration loop), so a same-tool same-args repeat within one turn hashes identically too — the old guard silently dropped the SECOND row on TODAY's v0.9.8, single-hook-family, no transition shim anywhere in play, corrupting the very telemetry the consolidation program's retirement decisions depend on. Fixed by making the guard **family-aware**: it now counts firings per `(key, hook family)`, family derived from `current_filter()`'s prefix (`desktop_mode_` vs `openstation_`), and suppresses a firing only when the OTHER family has fired MORE times for that key than THIS family has — a same-family repeat's own count only ever grows when it records, so it can never trip that condition; a true future both-families transition shim still collapses to exactly one recorded row per event. Two now-FALSE inline comments claiming the guard "only matters if a future release ever ships both as a transition shim" were corrected in both consumer files. **MEDIUM**: `openstation_resolve_script_payload()` (real post-#475 `payload.php:1371-1449`) resolves only a script handle's own `src`, never walks its declared deps, and server-sync/command-sync inject one bare `<script src="...">` tag per URL — so the `sn-desktop-mode-os-compat` prelude's `wp_register_script` dependency edges guarantee nothing on that lazy-load path. A post-#475 mid-session shell activation could load a widget file or `desktop-mode.js` before the prelude ever ran, leaving `window.openStationWidgets` (the name upstream actually reads) empty and every Cmd+K command dead until reload. Fixed by making every consumer **self-sufficient**: all 8 widget files' single-line `window.desktopModeWidgets = window.desktopModeWidgets || {}` prologue became a 3-statement merge-and-alias onto ONE object under both names (survivor = `openStationWidgets`, the name upstream reads; a genuine both-populated-and-differing race copies the loser's keys in first), and `assets/desktop-mode.js`'s gate now accepts either `window.wp.desktop` or `window.wp.os` and self-aliases `window.wp.desktop` locally so its 65 existing call sites keep working unchanged. The prelude itself is kept (print-order tidiness on the ordinary WP-enqueued boot path) but its docblock's false "always in place first, on either OpenStation line" claim — and the matching claim in `inc/desktop-mode-integration.php` — are corrected to state the lazy-load gap explicitly. **LOWs**: the `rest_prepare_plugin` icon-URL belt (`desktop_mode_icon_url`, v2.1.7's "ALWAYS override") now dual-writes `openstation_icon_url` too — the REST field's JSON *key* renames post-#475, a different seam from the already-dual-registered `plugins_window_icon_url` *filter* that only supplies the field's value; two `payload.php` line citations (`:213`→`:212`, `:1138`→`:1137`) corrected across the docs table and both inline comments; the system-prompt-appendix filter now registers with `accepted_args=2`, cheap future-proofing for the real call site's unused second arg. ([tests/openstation-compat.php](tests/openstation-compat.php) 54 asserts (+14), [tests/mcp-telemetry-agents.php](tests/mcp-telemetry-agents.php) 69 (+4), [tests/ai-tool-invocation-log.php](tests/ai-tool-invocation-log.php) 32 (+3), [tests/desktop-mode-integration.php](tests/desktop-mode-integration.php) 368 (+31) — every fix RED-pinned before the code change, all green after. Full sweep: 378 files, 14,324 assertions (+52), 0 failures. `composer phpstan` 316/316 files clean. `composer lint` clean.)

## [10.42.0] - 2026-08-04

### Added

- **`sn_apply` gains `change.type: "restore_revision"` — the acceptance path for the PR pattern** ([inc/sn-apply-restore-revision.php](inc/sn-apply-restore-revision.php), MCP consolidation session 7, `SNT_SN_APPLY_CHANGE_TYPES` 9 → 10). `mode:"revision"` responses have advertised `rollback:{method:'restore_revision', revision_id}` since v10.40.0, but no MCP path could execute a restore — accepting a staged revision meant classic wp-admin or WP-CLI. Worse, the staged-meta queue (`snt_sn_apply_stage_meta()`, session 6a) had no application path anywhere: a human restoring via wp-admin applies the content revision and strands queued meta in `wp_options` forever, since the Restore button knows nothing about SN's own queue. This is the first application path for it. **Publish-only**, via the exact structural mechanism `og_card`/`anchor_sweep` already use to refuse `mode:"revision"` — a restore IS the live write (the acceptance step); "staging a restore" would stage a revision of a revision. A routine credential is refused at gate 3 by the SAME identity grant every other publish-only type already goes through — zero new identity code. **Structural pre-check, before any gate runs**: the revision named in `payload.revision_id` must exist (`wp_get_post_revision()`, which collapses "missing" and "wrong post_type" to the same `null` — real 6.9 source read directly, the 6a lesson applied again before building rather than after) and belong to the target `post_id`; a foreign-parent revision refuses 409 naming both ids (the cross-target idempotency lesson generalized) — NOT restricted to sn_apply-staged revisions, since wp-admin lets a human restore any revision and narrowing below that buys nothing. **Gate 1 gets a REAL fingerprint scheme, not a skip** — required (missing → 422, distinct from mismatched → 409) and bound to the LIVE post's current `content_hash` (`snt_corpus_content_hash()`, reused verbatim from `inc/corpus-inspect.php` — the same value `sn_posts` exposes to callers), so a restore proposed against a since-edited post is the stale-branch merge conflict. **Gate 2 validates the REVISION's own fields** (`body` always, `excerpt` when non-empty — `post_title` has no check family anywhere in this codebase, honestly left unchecked rather than inventing one), never the live post's current state. **The write step self-guarantees its own rollback**: `wp_restore_post_revision()` guarantees nothing about a pre-restore snapshot (real 6.9 source: the pre-restore state survives only if the last writer happened to leave a matching revision row), so before restoring, the newest existing revision's three allowlisted fields are compared against live — reused as the rollback point if they already match (never duplicated), or a fresh snapshot of live's current state is staged via session 6a's `snt_sn_apply_stage_revision()` (never touches the live row) if they don't. The response's `rollback` always points at that snapshot — never at the revision that was just restored, which would re-apply the restore rather than undo it. Then the existing `snt_sn_apply_restore_revision()` wrapper promotes the revision to live, and — if `apply_staged_meta` (default **true**: the entire reason this change type exists is that wp-admin's Restore can't touch the queue, so a `false` default would silently reproduce that exact stranding for most real callers; `dry_run`, unchanged and still defaulting true, remains the actual human-review gate) — every staged-meta row for the same post is applied via `update_post_meta()` and its option row deleted, via a new per-post index maintained additively inside `snt_sn_apply_stage_meta()` itself (existing callers' return shape byte-unchanged). The index is honestly bounded: rows staged before it existed (v10.40.0–v10.41.2) are not enumerable by it — documented, not hidden, since the queue is designed to be accepted or discarded within the session it was proposed in. Result carries `{post_id, restored_revision_id, rollback_revision_id, meta_applied}` alongside the standard envelope; `dry_run:true` (default) runs all gates plus a `{before,after,fields_changed}` diff via the existing `snt_sn_apply_revision_diff()`, zero writes. Watched RED (free, structural): adding the 10th type to `SNT_SN_APPLY_CHANGE_TYPES` immediately REDed `tests/abilities-sn-apply-delegation-sweep.php`'s own ALL-TYPES sweep (`SWEEP.0: expected 10, got 9`) until the sweep table gained its own entry. A second, genuine finding surfaced writing this session's own tests: `snt_sn_apply_target_error_response()` (shared by every change type's target-resolution refusal, not new) never carried the underlying `WP_Error`'s own message into the response it builds — for a single-target call that response becomes the caller-facing error's entire message, so a carefully-worded "revision belongs to a different post" detail was being silently dropped before ever reaching the client; fixed with an additive `message` key, benefiting every type's target-error response, not just this one. ([tests/abilities-sn-apply-restore-revision.php](tests/abilities-sn-apply-restore-revision.php) → 74 asserts at initial ship, 93 after the review-round fixes below: structural mode refusal with the honest reason, routine-credential refusal at gate 3, missing/foreign-parent revision 404/409, missing/mismatched fingerprint 422/409, gate-2 findings proven to read the REVISION's content via a drift-lexicon phrase present only there, dry_run zero-writes with the diff shape, rollback-snapshot staged-vs-reused in both directions, restore verified end-to-end through the real wrapper, staged-meta applied + cleared + reported, an unrelated attachment's own staged meta left untouched, idempotent replay plus cross-target freshness. [tests/abilities-sn-apply-delegation-sweep.php](tests/abilities-sn-apply-delegation-sweep.php) 73 → 79.)

**Adversarial review REJECTed the first cut** (REJECT #10) on one HIGH and three MEDIUMs, all fixed in-worktree before this entry shipped, watched-RED first for every behavioral change. **HIGH**: gate 1's `$fingerprint` local was built with `isset()`, which collapses "fingerprint key absent" and "fingerprint key present, value `''`" to the identical `''` — but `snt_corpus_content_hash()` returns exactly `''` (never `md5('')`) for a blanked/whitespace-only post, the SAME value a caller legitimately observes via `sn_posts` for a blanked live post. Every honest, explicitly-passed `''` was silently reinterpreted as "missing" (422), so the disaster-recovery restore — this gate's own advertised use — was structurally impossible; nothing could ever pass. Fixed by detecting "missing" via `array_key_exists( 'fingerprint', $change )`, this codebase's documented present-vs-null idiom, instead of the shared `isset()`-collapsed local — an explicit `''` now reaches `hash_equals()` like any other value, while a genuinely absent key still 422s. **MEDIUM**: the rollback-snapshot pick (`$revisions[0]`) could anchor to an AUTOSAVE — real core explicitly skips autosaves when grabbing "the latest revision" (`wp_save_post_revision()`, `wp-includes/revision.php:165`, WP 6.9 source fetched and read directly) because autosave rows are rewritten IN PLACE by the next editor autosave, which would silently invalidate an autosave-anchored rollback pointer; now skipped via core's own `post_name` idiom (`str_contains( $post_name, "{$post_id}-revision" )`), copied verbatim. **MEDIUM ×2 (docs only)**: this bullet's own description previously implied alt_text's staged rows are applied by this path — false, they're queued under the ATTACHMENT id, which `restore_revision`'s `{post_id}` target structurally never resolves, so they remain stranded with no application path today (corrected here and in the ability description); and `docs/mcp-consolidation/FINDINGS.md`'s deviations list was missing a real deviation (staged-meta rows are applied unconditionally, never re-checked for fingerprint staleness — the stored fingerprint is opaque by design and `surfaces`' postmeta fields have no comparable scheme at all) plus undercounted its own list by two, both fixed. **Pre-existing, attempted and landed**: a `dry_run:true` call carrying an `idempotency_key` was recorded into (and replayable from) the idempotency store, so the natural dry-run-diff-then-apply workflow this very change type documents — preview, then `dry_run:false` under the same key — replayed the untouched preview forever instead of ever executing the write. Grepped every existing `idempotency_key` use across `tests/*.php` first: none pairs a key with `dry_run:true`, so no shipped pin asserted the broken behavior and the fix was safe to land, minimal and one-directional — `dry_run:true` now skips the idempotency lookup and record entirely (a preview always runs fresh), while a genuine `dry_run:false` call's behavior — lookup, record, replay — is completely unchanged; affects all 10 change types uniformly, since the fix lives in the shared `snt_ability_sn_apply()` entry point, not per-type code. ([tests/abilities-sn-apply-restore-revision.php](tests/abilities-sn-apply-restore-revision.php) +19 asserts for the HIGH/MEDIUM-1 fixes; [tests/abilities-sn-apply.php](tests/abilities-sn-apply.php) 52 → 62, +10 for the idempotency fix. Full account, including exact watched-RED output for each fix, in `docs/mcp-consolidation/FINDINGS.md`'s "Review round — REJECT #10".) Full sweep: 377 files, 14,183 assertions, 0 failures (up from 376/14,074 pre-session, 14,154 at initial ship). PHPStan (315 files) clean. PHPCS clean.

## [10.41.2] - 2026-08-04

### Fixed

- **Staged revisions were backdated to the parent's last-modified date — Restore silently disabled in wp-admin** ([inc/sn-apply-revision.php](inc/sn-apply-revision.php)). Owner-observed live: `sn_apply`'s `mode:"revision"` staged a real WordPress revision (post 1721, rev 2138), but clicking Restore in wp-admin was a silent no-op — the live post never changed. Root cause, confirmed against the real WP 7.0.2 source (`wp-includes/revision.php:92-93`): core's `_wp_post_revision_data()` sets the REVISION row's `post_date`/`post_date_gmt` from whatever `post_modified`/`post_modified_gmt` sit on the array it's handed. Every core caller of that helper runs it post-update — `wp_save_post_revision()` fires from `save_post`, after `wp_update_post()` has already stamped the parent's `post_modified` to "now" — so the field means "now" at the moment core reads it. `snt_sn_apply_stage_revision()` (session 6a, v10.40.0) runs at a different moment: staging deliberately never touches the live row, so it handed core the LIVE row's `post_modified` verbatim — the post's last genuine edit, which can be days old. The staged revision inherited that stale date, collided with (or predated) the newest genuine revision's own date, and wp-admin's revisions browser sorted the stale-dated staged revision as the CURRENT one — which disables Restore on the current revision by design. **Fix**: `snt_sn_apply_stage_revision()` now overrides `post_modified`/`post_modified_gmt` on the snapshot array to the actual staging moment (`current_time('mysql')` / `current_time('mysql', 1)`, the same idiom core itself uses when stamping an update) immediately before handing it to `_wp_put_post_revision()` — re-deriving the one context-dependent input core's helper assumes, for THIS call's moment rather than an update's. The live post row is still never written; only the array passed into the revision-insert path changes, so the byte-identical-live-row guarantee (acceptance test 6) is unaffected and re-verified. ([tests/sn-apply-revision.php](tests/sn-apply-revision.php) → 76 asserts, three new: Test 18 pins the staged revision's `post_date`/`post_date_gmt` to the injected staging time rather than a deliberately-stale parent `post_modified` fixture — watched RED against pre-fix code (4 assertions failed exactly as predicted, everything else stayed green); Test 19 pins ordering against a pre-existing revision row carrying the parent's old modified date, the exact collision that disabled Restore; Test 20 re-asserts the parent row stays byte-identical in the same stale-date scenario. `current_time()` stub added following the codebase's existing injectable-`$now` testability convention. Three sibling fixtures that also `require` `inc/sn-apply-revision.php` — [tests/abilities-sn-apply-batch-and-rollback.php](tests/abilities-sn-apply-batch-and-rollback.php), [tests/abilities-sn-apply-delegation-sweep.php](tests/abilities-sn-apply-delegation-sweep.php), [tests/abilities-sn-apply-type-coverage.php](tests/abilities-sn-apply-type-coverage.php) — fataled on `current_time()` undefined once the primitive started calling it; each gained the same stub.) Full sweep: 376 test files, lint clean, 0 failures. PHPStan (314 files) clean. PHPCS clean.

## [10.41.1] - 2026-08-04

### Fixed

- **`sn_apply`'s `target` reached the ability as a JSON string, failing every real call** ([inc/abilities-sn-apply.php](inc/abilities-sn-apply.php), [inc/abilities-sn-validate.php](inc/abilities-sn-validate.php)). Found on the first real MCP client call to v10.40.0's `sn_apply`: `input[target][0] is not of type object` on every call regardless of what the client sent (object and array forms both). Root cause, confirmed by reading `inc/mcp/mcp-tools.php`'s `sn_mcp_normalize_schema()` directly rather than assumed: `target`'s schema declared its object/array union as a nested `oneOf` with **no top-level `type` key at all** — `oneOf` was its only key. That shape survives this codebase's own normalizer untouched (it strips `oneOf`/`allOf`/`anyOf` at the schema **root** only, by design, so a strict host doesn't reject the whole tool over one property's real constraint), but the projected tool schema still shipped `"target": {}` to the client — and at least one real MCP client facing a parameter with no discoverable type serializes whatever it's given as a JSON **string** rather than structured JSON (the same transport-transform lesson as `wp_localize_script` string-casting every scalar: a stub, or here a schema, must model the transport's actual behavior, not just its happy path). **Fix, two layers**: (1) schema — `target` now declares `'type' => array( 'object', 'array' )` with `properties` (the object branch) and `items` (the array branch) side by side, instead of `oneOf`. A `type` array union is not a schema combinator; it is the exact pattern already load-bearing elsewhere in this codebase (`sn-posts`/`sn-scan`'s `cursor`, every nullable output field) and survives projection because there is nothing for `sn_mcp_normalize_schema()` — or any other layer — to strip. Runtime enforcement (`snt_sn_apply_resolve_target()`, `snt_sn_apply_is_batch_target()`) is byte-unchanged. (2) transport tolerance, defense in depth: `snt_ability_sn_apply()` now `json_decode()`s `target` when it arrives as a string before anything downstream sees it; an undecodable non-null string refuses 422 (`snt_sn_apply_bad_target_encoding`) rather than silently falling through to "target not resolved". **Sweep**: the fix's own projection-round-trip test, run over all five real registered CONSOLIDATED tools (`sn_posts`, `sn_site_facts`, `sn_scan`, `sn_validate`, `sn_apply` — `inc/mcp/mcp-capabilities.php`'s own count; there is no sixth tool registered anywhere in `inc/`), found `sn_validate`'s `checks` property with the **identical** untyped-`oneOf` shape — not independently reported live, but structurally the same live risk. Fixed the same way in the same session: `type => ['string','array']` replacing the `oneOf`, plus the matching string-decode tolerance in `snt_ability_sn_validate()` (checks:"all" as a bare string is untouched — only non-"all" strings attempt a decode). No other property across the five tools' input schemas triggered the sweep. ([tests/mcp-projection-schema-types.php](tests/mcp-projection-schema-types.php) — new, 31 asserts: runs the REAL registered ability through the REAL `sn_mcp_project_tool()` for all five consolidated tools and asserts every property in the projected schema carries a usable type, the exact assertion that would have caught this before ship; watched RED against the pre-fix schemas, reproducing both violations (`sn-apply.target`, `sn-validate.checks`) before the fix landed, then green. [tests/abilities-sn-apply.php](tests/abilities-sn-apply.php) 46 → 52 asserts: acceptance tests 1b/1c cover the JSON-string decode and the undecodable-string refusal. [tests/abilities-sn-validate.php](tests/abilities-sn-validate.php) 44 → 48 asserts: acceptance test 5b covers the same for `checks`, including that `checks:"all"` as a bare string is unaffected.) Full sweep: 376 files, 14,067 asserts, 0 failures. PHPStan (314 files) clean. PHPCS clean.

## [10.41.0] - 2026-08-04

The `## Label` textareas are replaced by the resume editor's card/row idiom (owner-approved design, parked 2026-08-03): section/group cards with a label field and repeatable item rows — Uses items split the name/note pair into two fields — reusing the sn-rsm JS/CSS shipped in v10.33.0. The text document STAYS the stored format: on save the handlers serialize the posted rows back into the same `## Label` text ([inc/admin-post-actions.php](inc/admin-post-actions.php) `sn_now_rows_to_text()`/`sn_uses_rows_to_text()`) and ride `sn_now_page_save()`/`sn_uses_page_save()` unchanged — data layers, sync engines, migrations, flash codes, and edge-purge behavior all untouched, and the legacy `now_content`/`uses_content` string path stays test-pinned. ## [10.40.0] - 2026-08-04

### Added

- **`sn_apply` revision-mode write primitive** ([inc/sn-apply-revision.php](inc/sn-apply-revision.php), MCP consolidation session 6a). `docs/mcp-consolidation/FINDINGS.md` #5 found that `mode: "revision"` — the sn_apply spec's core PR-pattern selling point — exists nowhere in the codebase: every existing apply ability (block-migrations-apply, pattern-adoption-apply, the ai-\*-apply family, update-post-surfaces) writes live via `wp_update_post()` only. This session builds that primitive in isolation, with no ability/tool registered and no gates wired — session 6b's job. Four functions: `snt_sn_apply_stage_revision()` stages post_content/post_title/post_excerpt as a genuine new WordPress revision via core's `_wp_put_post_revision()`, never touching the live post row (there is no code path here that calls `wp_update_post()` or `wp_insert_post()` with the parent's own ID); `snt_sn_apply_stage_meta()`/`snt_sn_apply_get_staged_meta()` are a separate, explicitly-not-postmeta draft queue (one wp_options row per post_id+meta_key) for the future meta-writing change types (surfaces, og_card, alt_text) that core revisions can't carry without a per-key `revisions_enabled` audit this session didn't scope; `snt_sn_apply_restore_revision()` wraps `wp_restore_post_revision()`; `snt_sn_apply_revision_diff()` reports before/after/fields_changed against the current live post. Grounded against the real WP 7.0.2 core source (cached and read directly, not recalled — see the file's own docblock): `_wp_put_post_revision()`'s field allowlist is `post_title`/`post_content`/`post_excerpt` **only** — `post_author` is explicitly on that function's own disallowed-field list, never a revisioned field. `_wp_put_post_revision()` calls `wp_insert_post( $post, true )` **with** `$wp_error = true`, so a DB failure surfaces as a real `WP_Error` (the primitive's `is_wp_error()` check is the primary path; a defensive `empty()` fallback stays for cross-version safety, not because `0` is the documented shape). Core also runs `wp_slash()` on the row before inserting — the primitive passes its snapshot through raw/unslashed on purpose, so core's single slashing pass isn't doubled. On the hook-cascade question: **`save_post`/`save_post_{type}` fire unconditionally for revision inserts too** — there is no core-level post_type guard, contrary to this session's first pass — and so do `transition_post_status` and `wp_insert_post`. Every safety property here comes from the plugin's OWN guards: `inc/schedule-sync.php` and `inc/post-settings.php` both check `wp_is_post_revision()` before doing anything on `save_post`; all five of the plugin's `transition_post_status` hooks (ml-artifacts, ai-prepopulate, indexnow, webhooks, websub) guard on post-type/publish-status. A revision-disabled post type or `wp_revisions_to_keep() === 0` errors loudly here (WP_Error, never silent) — deliberately bypassing `wp_save_post_revision()`, which silently no-ops in both cases. ([tests/sn-apply-revision.php](tests/sn-apply-revision.php) → 69 asserts, including a permanent RED-control test proving the byte-identical assertion catches a live-write mechanism, a slash-safety test against gnarly content, and both the `WP_Error` and defensive-`0` failure branches of `wp_insert_post()`.)
- **`sn_apply` — the consolidated write tool** ([inc/abilities-sn-apply.php](inc/abilities-sn-apply.php), [inc/sn-apply-gates.php](inc/sn-apply-gates.php), [inc/sn-apply-validation.php](inc/sn-apply-validation.php), [inc/sn-apply-executors.php](inc/sn-apply-executors.php), MCP consolidation session 6b — `signal-noise/sn-apply`, rw door 35 → 36). Registered NEW alongside every ability it absorbs (block-migrations-apply, pattern-adoption-apply, ai-alt-apply, ai-drift-apply, ai-link-apply, update-post-surfaces, regenerate-og-card, anchor-sweep — none touched, unregistered, or deleted). Four gates run in this exact order, every one reporting `{passed,...}` even when an earlier gate already failed: **1. fingerprint** — reuses each absorbed impl's own scheme (the shared block-fingerprint engine for block_migration/pattern_adoption, `snt_ai_drift_fingerprint()`/`snt_ai_drift_locate_in_raw()` for drift_replace/link_insert); alt_text/surfaces/og_card/anchor_sweep have no fingerprint scheme in their absorbed impl and report `skipped:'no_fingerprint_scheme'` rather than fabricating one. **2. server-side validation** — calls `sn_validate`'s own per-surface check functions directly (`snt_sn_validate_check_alt_text`/`_links`/`_body`/`_excerpt`/`_meta_description`/`_og_card_title`), never the full `sn_validate` ability wrapper (its corpus-post gate would reject alt_text's attachment target outright); og_card/anchor_sweep have no applicable check family and report `skipped:'no_applicable_checks'`. **3. mode capability** — a NEW ability-level layer on top of the rw door's existing hardening (kill switch/credential-split/rate-limit/audit, all inherited unmodified): `sn_apply_granted_modes` filter, default `['revision','publish']` for the rw door's bound owner credential (reusing `sn_mcp_rw_bound_uuid()`/`sn_mcp_rw_authenticated_app_password_uuid()`, never a parallel identity scheme) and `['revision']` for anyone else — combined with a STRUCTURAL mode-support matrix per change type (`snt_sn_apply_mode_support()`): og_card (`sn_generate_og_card()` writes a PNG FILE, not a post field) and anchor_sweep (a live HTTP dispatch to the provenance Worker, no post entity at all) are publish-only and refuse `mode:"revision"` even for the owner, with the reason surfaced verbatim rather than faking a staged version of an unstageable side effect. **4. idempotency** — a new bounded option row (`snt_sn_apply_idempotency_log`, autoload false, 500-row cap, 14-day retention, age-then-count prune mirroring the rw audit log's own pattern), keyed TARGET-SCOPED per adversarial review (one HIGH, fixed in-worktree, watched-RED first): the store key is `sha256('sn_apply|' + idempotency_key + '|' + canonical_target)` where the canonical target (`post:812` / `attachment:400` / `scope:provenance_anchors`, batches sorted-joined) is derived from the raw request shape — a duplicate `(key, target)` pair returns the FIRST call's full response verbatim (`replayed:true`), never re-executing, even with a different payload, while the SAME key reused on a DIFFERENT target is simply a fresh execution (idempotency protects the retry of the same logical call, never a cross-target dedupe; the pre-fix global key replayed target A's response for a target-B call). Belt-and-braces, each stored row also records its canonical target and a mismatch on replay refuses with `snt_sn_apply_idempotency_target_mismatch` (409) naming both targets. `dry_run` defaults to true; a dry run runs all four gates and produces a diff via a read-only preview path (gate 1's own `snt_sn_apply_compute_block_replacement()`/substr_replace preview, never the write path) with a DB-verified zero-writes guard. `mode:"revision"` routes each write-capable absorbed impl's WRITE STEP (not its validation) through session 6a's `snt_sn_apply_stage_revision()`/`snt_sn_apply_stage_meta()` via a new optional `write_callback` parameter threaded additively into `snt_block_fp_apply()`, `snt_ai_drift_apply_impl()`, and `snt_ai_link_apply_impl()` — every existing caller omits it, so legacy behavior (`block-migrations-apply`, `pattern-adoption-apply`, `ai-drift-apply`, `ai-link-apply`) is byte-for-byte unchanged (all four abilities' own test suites re-verified green). `target` accepts a single object or a batch array: per-post writes are atomic, across posts they're independent (one target's 404/409/422 never rolls back another), response is a `{batch, results[], summary}` shape for arrays and the spec's single-target shape otherwise. Refusals return `WP_Error` with `array('status'=>N)` (409 fingerprint, 422 validation, 403 capability) carrying the full gates/diff payload JSON-encoded in the message — the EXISTING `sn_mcp_call_tool()` plumbing (untouched) already turns any ability-level `WP_Error` into an `isError:true` tool result and already calls `sn_mcp_rw_audit_record()` for every rw-door outcome; this ability rides an ADDITIONAL, explicit call of its own (widening `sn_mcp_rw_audit_safe_arg_keys()` with 11 new scalar keys — change_type/mode/dry_run/candidate_id/applied/replayed/revision_id/the four gate-passed booleans) purely because gate outcomes and revision_id are OUTPUT, never visible to the door's own args-only redaction. ([tests/abilities-sn-apply.php](tests/abilities-sn-apply.php) → 46 asserts, acceptance tests 1-5 plus the review-HIGH's cross-target 4b/4c cases; [tests/abilities-sn-apply-batch-and-rollback.php](tests/abilities-sn-apply-batch-and-rollback.php) → 35 asserts, acceptance tests 6-8 including the mode:"revision" byte-identical crown jewel driven through the FULL tool path; [tests/abilities-sn-apply-type-coverage.php](tests/abilities-sn-apply-type-coverage.php) → 42 asserts, review MEDIUM-2 coverage for surfaces/og_card/anchor_sweep including dedicated PNG-regen and Worker-dispatch call recorders; [tests/abilities-sn-apply-delegation-sweep.php](tests/abilities-sn-apply-delegation-sweep.php) → 67 asserts, pattern_adoption + link_insert delegation pins via the absorbed impls' own error codes plus the ALL-EIGHT-types structural dry_run zero-writes sweep looping the enum itself.)
- **`sn_apply` gains `change.type: "create_draft"`** ([inc/sn-apply-create-draft.php](inc/sn-apply-create-draft.php), MCP consolidation session 6c — the arc's finale, `SNT_SN_APPLY_CHANGE_TYPES` 8 → 9). Closes `docs/mcp-consolidation/FINDINGS.md` session 1's #(b): "`create-draft` has zero code; `sn_apply`'s target union has no 'new post' variant." Origin: an owner ask — "put it in the drafts" — that was structurally impossible with no create-post ability on the surface at all; DRAFT status only, never publish/future/schedule, the owner schedules by hand. `target` gains a 4th shape, `{new_post:true}` (no id — the post doesn't exist yet); its canonical idempotency identity is CONTENT-derived (`'new_post:' + sha256(title+content)`, `snt_sn_apply_canonical_target()`'s new optional `$change` parameter) rather than the other 8 types' target-identity scheme, so an identical retry replays but a genuinely different draft is always fresh, even under the same `idempotency_key`. **Mode semantics are its own, not a reuse of "revision"**: `mode:"publish"` refuses STRUCTURALLY at gate 3 (`snt_sn_apply_mode_support()`) — the exact mechanism og_card/anchor_sweep already use to refuse `mode:"revision"`, mirrored — reason states plainly that drafts are scheduled by hand. `mode:"revision"` is the ONE supported mode, but does NOT route through session 6a's `snt_sn_apply_stage_revision()` primitive (there is no parent post to stage a core revision against); it dispatches to its own write primitive, `snt_sn_apply_write_create_draft()`, a real `wp_insert_post()` with `post_status` hard-coded `'draft'` and `post_type` hard-coded `'post'` — never taken from the payload, never `wp_publish_post()`. Gate 2 assembles findings from real `sn_validate` check families (excerpt/tags/body — the last carrying `block_pattern_registered`) plus two checks unique to a create: forbidden payload fields (`post_status`/`post_date`/`post_type` are rejected 422, naming the field — accepting any would let a caller quietly defeat the draft-only guarantee) and a NEW deterministic block-comment DELIMITER balance check (`snt_sn_apply_block_delimiter_findings()`, PCRE recursion for nested JSON attrs, mirrors the block parser's own frame-stack shape) — `parse_blocks()` alone does not catch malformed delimiters (WP's parser is lenient and silently treats them as freeform HTML). Title capped at 200 chars, content at 256 KB — both NEW, documented-not-measured ceilings (no live corpus access this session; flagged for a follow-up recalibration against real data). Tags are existing-vocabulary-only, enforced at TWO independent layers: gate 2 reuses `snt_sn_validate_check_tags()`, and the write primitive independently resolves every proposed name to an existing `term_id` via the new `snt_sn_apply_resolve_tag_ids()` (same `sn_tag_normalize_key()`/`get_terms()` lookup, never a parallel scheme) before calling `wp_set_post_tags()` with INTEGER ids only, never raw names — `wp_set_post_tags()` creates a new term for any unmatched STRING (`$append` controls association replacement, not creation), so a gate-2-only enforcement would have let a regression, normalization mismatch, or race silently invent vocabulary (caught in adversarial review, fixed in-worktree before ship). An id that fails to resolve refuses 422 BEFORE `wp_insert_post()` runs, so a bad tag never orphans a draft. Gate 1 (fingerprint) honestly reports `skipped:'no_fingerprint_scheme'` — nothing exists yet to fingerprint. Result carries `{post_id, edit_link, status:'draft'}`; rollback is `{method:'delete_draft', post_id}` (a draft delete is trash, reversible) — `snt_ability_sn_apply()`'s rollback-shaping gains a `create_draft`-specific branch since the generic `revision_id`-keyed branch never fires here (`revision_id` stays `null`). Compared with the desktop-mode plugin's `desktop-mode/create-post` reference implementation (v0.9.8): both are draft-only by construction and author as the calling identity; this tool is STRICTER on content integrity (delimiter-balance validation before insert vs. desktop-mode's `wp_kses_post()` sanitize-and-hope, despite its own docblock claiming "content is stored RAW"), stricter on size (explicit title/content caps vs. none), and adds retry-safety (content-derived idempotency vs. none — a desktop-mode retry duplicates the draft) and an explicit rollback contract (vs. none); it is LOOSER on post_type (post only, vs. desktop-mode's post/page choice) and has no tag support in desktop-mode's schema to compare against. Watched RED (free, structural): adding the 9th type to `SNT_SN_APPLY_CHANGE_TYPES` immediately REDs `tests/abilities-sn-apply-delegation-sweep.php`'s `SWEEP.0` enum-count pin (8 ≠ 9) until the sweep table gains its own `create_draft` case — captured, then closed by adding that case. ([tests/abilities-sn-apply-create-draft.php](tests/abilities-sn-apply-create-draft.php) → 83 asserts: draft lands with status draft + correct author, forbidden-field rejection naming each field, publish-mode structural refusal with the honest reason, unclosed/mismatched/balanced block-delimiter cases, tag-vocabulary enforcement including the real `wp_set_post_tags()` call, idempotent replay vs. content-derived fresh execution, dry_run zero-inserts under the write-call recorder, both size caps, the honest fingerprint skip, and the `WP_Error` `wp_insert_post()` failure shape — its defensive `empty()`/int-0 arm was deliberately NOT built: this repo's pinned WP 7.0 stubs narrow `wp_insert_post( $args, true )`'s success type to `int<1, max>`, so PHPStan correctly flags that check as dead code, unlike `_wp_put_post_revision()`'s plainer, unrefined stub which keeps 6a's defensive arm legitimate.)

## [10.39.0] - 2026-08-04

### Added

- **Rights-signal anchoring check — the 18th Content Health check** ([inc/health-check-rights-anchored.php](inc/health-check-rights-anchored.php)). Three things watch the rights surface and none of them watched this one. The 14th check asks *is the live surface still correct?*; the ledger's own `verify:rights-signals` asks *is every anchored claim sound?* A provenance worker that silently stopped re-anchoring leaves **both green forever** — the live surface is still correct, and the old records are still perfectly valid. This check asks the third question: *has the surface being served right now been anchored at all?* It hashes the four live surfaces (`robots.txt`, `/.well-known/tdmrep.json`, `/license.xml`, `/tdm-policy/`) and compares each against the newest ledger record, read from the `rights_signals` section the provenance repo's `index.json` now publishes — one cheap read instead of probing `v1`, `v2`, … until a 404.

  Detection is deliberately **external rather than a worker heartbeat**: "sweep completed" is a success-only readout, and `anchorRightsSignals` has exactly that shape (a per-signal failure is caught, logged, and stepped over), so a heartbeat would report healthy while one surface never anchored.

  Divergence alone is not a fault — the worker anchors on an hourly tick, so a surface that changed minutes ago is legitimately unanchored. The check remembers when a divergence was **first seen** and only raises a finding once it outlives two sweeps (`SN_RIGHTS_ANCHOR_GRACE`, filterable via `sn_health_rights_anchor_grace`); a live hash that changes again re-stamps the clock, because that is a fresh edit rather than a stuck anchor. An unreachable ledger is an **advisory with zero findings** and leaves the remembered state untouched — overwriting it would silently restart every grace clock, so a permanently unreachable ledger could never accumulate a finding. A surface that fails to fetch is skipped, never accused: hashing a failed fetch would manufacture drift out of an outage. ([tests/health-check-rights-anchored.php](tests/health-check-rights-anchored.php) → 23 asserts, driving every timing path offline.)

## [10.38.0] - 2026-08-03

### Added

- **WP 7.1 ability-lifecycle guard** ([inc/abilities-lifecycle-guard.php](inc/abilities-lifecycle-guard.php)). WordPress 7.1 standardizes ability execution with core hooks (`wp_ability_invoked`, `wp_ability_permission_result`, `wp_ability_execute_result`). Until now every layer of our hardening — rw kill switch, telemetry, rw audit — was wired into the two MCP doors only, so abilities run through the native `/wp-abilities/v1/…/run` route or Desktop Mode reached their own `permission_callback` and nothing else. The guard attaches the same policy to the core hooks: **tighten-only** enforcement (an upstream denial is never flipped to allow; the READ switch is deliberately not extended — it governs the MCP transport, not the data), telemetry recorded under a new `direct` door so existing `read`/`rw` rows stay distinguishable, and rw audit rows for write-class executions. Write-class is derived from three signals — rw-allowlist membership, the ability's own `annotations` (`readonly`/`destructive`), and the four abilities held off *both* doors for blast radius (`run-cron-event`, `ai-orphan-apply`, `merge-tags`, `clear-template-overrides`) which remain REST-run-reachable and need the brake most. Inert pre-7.1: the hooks never fire. `sn_mcp_call_tool()` and the resources passthrough bracket their `execute()` calls with a dispatch-depth flag so MCP traffic is never double-recorded or mislabelled. ([tests/abilities-lifecycle-guard.php](tests/abilities-lifecycle-guard.php) → 47 asserts.)

### Changed

- **Schema client-prep delegates to core when WP 7.1 is present** ([inc/mcp/mcp-tools.php](inc/mcp/mcp-tools.php) `sn_mcp_normalize_schema`). `wp_prepare_json_schema_for_client()` runs first behind a `function_exists` guard — it strips server-only keywords (`sanitize_callback`/`validate_callback`/`arg_options`) and hoists property-level `required` into Draft-4 arrays, neither of which we ever did. Our three provider-specific fixes (scalar `type: object`, top-level combinator strip, empty-properties `{}`) are a different contract with strict MCP hosts and stay layered on top. Pre-7.1 behavior is byte-identical, asserted in the same process before the stub exists. ([tests/mcp-schema-client-prep.php](tests/mcp-schema-client-prep.php) → 12 asserts.)

### Fixed

- **List-table cell lookup future-proofed** ([assets/health-suggest-actions.js](assets/health-suggest-actions.js)). `closest('td')` → `closest('td,th')`. WP 7.1 moves the post-list-table row header from the checkbox cell to the title cell; this script only ever runs on plugin-owned tables, so nothing breaks today — the widened selector removes the coupling entirely. Audit found no other list-table selector exposure in either repo.
