## [10.34.0] - 2026-08-03

### Added

- **`Content-Signal` TDM header now travels on every REST response** ([inc/rest-hardening-policy.php](inc/rest-hardening-policy.php)). A REST authorization audit found the rights-reservation stack was incomplete on the machine-readable surface: `TDM-Reservation` and `TDM-Policy` already shipped (v9.83.0), but `Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-train=no, ai-input=yes` — the TDMRep / Content Signals grammar declaring *index yes, train no, retrieve yes* — was missing. It now emits on every namespace via `rest_post_dispatch`. All three values are `defined()`-guarded constants (`SN_TDM_RESERVATION`, `SN_TDM_POLICY_URL`, `SN_TDM_CONTENT_SIGNAL`) overridable in wp-config and still refinable through the `snt_rest_hardening_policy` filter. ([tests/rest-hardening.php](tests/rest-hardening.php) pins all three.)
- **Per-user courtesy throttle for expensive abilities** ([inc/abilities-rate-gate.php](inc/abilities-rate-gate.php)). The native Abilities run-route (`/wp-abilities/v1/.../run`) has no rate limit of its own — only the MCP write door does — so a runaway automation loop could hammer a work-heavy ability unbounded. New `snt_ability_rate_gate()` (per-user, fixed-count-per-window transient, fail-open without the transient API) now guards `near-duplicate-scan` (O(n²) pair comparison) and `run-insights-scan` (forced scan does real work each call). `run-narration` is intentionally excluded — it is an async, deduped background trigger. Not a security boundary (every gated ability already requires `manage_options`); caps are a generous 10/60s and filterable via `snt_ability_rate_gate_max` / `_window`. ([tests/abilities-rate-gate.php](tests/abilities-rate-gate.php), 11 asserts.)

Full route/ability inventory (15 native routes + 65 abilities), findings by severity, and a runnable prod-facing curl sequence. ## [10.33.1] - 2026-08-03

### Fixed

- **/resume lost its layout after the v10.33.0 takeover save — the body is now REAL serialized block markup, not wp:html** ([inc/resume-sync-engine.php](inc/resume-sync-engine.php)). ## [10.33.0] - 2026-08-03

### Added

- **/resume structured editor — Content → Resume Page** ([inc/resume-page.php](inc/resume-page.php), [inc/resume-sync-engine.php](inc/resume-sync-engine.php), [inc/admin-forms/resume-page.php](inc/admin-forms/resume-page.php), [assets/resume-admin.js](assets/resume-admin.js)). Owner ask: an easy way to update the resume from wp-admin that is *not* a plain-text box like Now/Uses and not hand-edited blocks. The live page's hand-authored block markup had already drifted — the credentials section's delimiters were scrambled (missing `/wp:heading` closer, a `/wp:heading` where `/wp:column` belongs, doubled `/wp:group` at EOF), one editor-open away from "Attempt block recovery".

  Architecture mirrors the Now/Uses regenerate-on-save engines, with a STRUCTURED form instead of a text grammar:

  - **Data layer**: one durable autoload=no option (`sn_resume_doc`) holds the canonical document — hero (summary/chips/contact/PDF), stats, experience (employers → roles → bullets), the earlier-career fold, education, affiliations, publications, skills. `sn_resume_doc_normalize()` canonicalises or REFUSES: unknown keys dropped, blank rows pruned and reindexed, URLs http(s)-only, and a document with neither an experience entry nor a publication is never saved — a bad POST can never blank the live page. Bullets are the one HTML-bearing field (`<strong>`/`<em>`/`<a>` via `wp_kses` at normalize); every other string is plain text escaped at the render sink. Before the first save, the editor prefills from a shipped seed ([inc/seed-content/resume-data.json](inc/seed-content/resume-data.json)) transcribed verbatim from the live page's 720 words — zero content loss at takeover.
  - **Sync engine**: every real save regenerates the /resume Page body as ONE `wp:html` freeform block reproducing the live design's markup (same `sn-resume-*` / preset classes and inline styles). `wp:html` carries no validation semantics, so the generated body can never trigger block recovery — the drift class of bug dies structurally, and the first save repairs the existing scramble as a side effect. `post_content` keeps real text, so word counts, corpus tools, excerpts, and schema.org `wordCount` all keep working (the shortcode alternative was rejected for exactly this). Excerpt is seeded only when empty, never overwritten.
  - **Form**: sectioned, collapsible cards with repeatable rows — add/remove/reorder for chips, stats, employers, roles, bullets, education/affiliation lines, publications, and skills rows. A new paper is three fields and Save. Row mechanics live in self-gating vanilla JS ([assets/resume-admin.js](assets/resume-admin.js), no-op without `[data-rsm-add]`, the analytics-brush precedent): templates bake placeholder tokens for nested lists and the JS swaps every occurrence for a unique key at clone time — nested `<template>` content included, via `template.content` traversal (no innerHTML writes). PHP receives string array keys and reindexes at normalize, so key contiguity never matters.
  - **Handler**: `sn_action=resume_save` ([inc/admin-post-actions.php](inc/admin-post-actions.php)) — `wp_unslash` before the data layer (the update_option slash asymmetry; apostrophes gain no backslashes, test-pinned), refusal → `resume_refused` with the live page untouched, real saves purge `/resume` (both slash variants). +1 dispatch-map action (51). Flash codes: saved / unchanged / refused / failed.

  Tests: [tests/resume-page.php](tests/resume-page.php) (31 asserts: normalize discipline, refusal anchors, seed round-trip, wp_date stamp, autoload=no, seed fallback), [tests/resume-sync-engine.php](tests/resume-sync-engine.php) (34: body markers for every section, div/section balance, "no other block delimiters are generated — nothing left to scramble", upsert/excerpt semantics), [tests/resume-admin-form.php](tests/resume-admin-form.php) (27: input names mirror the document shape, every add-button has its template+list, token discipline incl. the nested-template `__E__`/`__R__` collision case, tag balance), plus the resume_save group in [tests/admin-post-actions.php](tests/admin-post-actions.php) (13: flash paths, purge variants, string-keyed JS rows, refusal leaves the store intact). [tests/admin-registry.php](tests/admin-registry.php) updated for the new Content leaf.

## [10.32.0] - 2026-08-02

### Changed

- **Cron cadence flags are now burst-resistant — the trailing-50-firings window is a COUNT, not a duration** ([inc/ml-cadence.php](inc/ml-cadence.php), [inc/ml-kernel.php](inc/ml-kernel.php)). The health check produced **five false findings on 2026-08-02** after the weekend release marathon: activity-coupled hooks (`wp_version_check`, `sn_verify_auto_purge`, `sn_analytics_rollup`, `od_trigger_page_cache_invalidation`, `snt_ml_rebuild_async`) fired every ~9–60 minutes during the burst, so the whole window collapsed into ~36 hours, the learner adopted a burst as the baseline, and the next ordinary quiet day z-flagged all five. The observed absurdity: `wp_version_check` flagged at **z 13.89 on a 6.4h gap while its registered schedule is `twicedaily` (12h)** — flagged late while not yet due. Four changes, one-sided late-only as before, with **no suppression state and no configuration UI**:

  1. **No schedule, no expectation.** A hook with no registered recurrence — the `wp_schedule_single_event()` on-demand hooks (`sn_analytics_rollup`'s SWR warmer at [inc/analytics-rollup.php:888](inc/analytics-rollup.php), `snt_ml_rebuild_async` at [inc/ml-artifacts.php:261](inc/ml-artifacts.php)) — is watched and never flagged. Their firing rhythm tracks admin visits and publishes, not cron health. This adopts the position [inc/cron-dashboard.php:491](inc/cron-dashboard.php) already took for its own staleness math (`snt_cron_hook_is_on_demand()`) rather than re-deriving it; the ML detector had been the only surface judging on-demand hooks as if they were scheduled.
  2. **Schedule floor.** A hook never flags below `SNT_ML_CADENCE_FLOOR_FACTOR` (1.5) × its registered interval, read from `snt_cron_interval_seconds()`. The registration is ground truth and a learner may not undercut it — this alone retires the `wp_version_check` finding.
  3. **Robust statistics.** The cron path moved from EWMA/population-σ to **median/MAD** via the new pure kernel function `snt_ml_cadence_deviation_robust()`. Mean/σ has a breakdown point of 0 (one burst drags the expectation down *and* collapses the spread, so the denominator explodes); median/MAD's is 50%. The publish path keeps EWMA — twenty posts span months, so the failure mode does not exist there.
  4. **Window-span trust.** A window is believed only once it spans `SNT_ML_CADENCE_MIN_SPAN` (7 days) of wall-clock, **or** its learned median is at least `SNT_ML_CADENCE_AGREE_FACTOR` (0.5) × the registered interval. The second leg is what keeps coverage for legitimately frequent hooks: 50 firings of an hourly job can never span a week, so a span-only rule would blind the detector to them permanently.

  Rules 1 and 4 are deliberately separate: **adversarial review REJECTed the first cut on exactly this** — a hook firing in daily clusters (five firings per weekday) spans months while its median gap stays minutes, so span alone would have re-admitted the poisoned window for precisely the on-demand hooks named in the incident, two of which get `interval_s = 0` because `wp_get_schedule()` returns `false` for single events. The same review caught a second HIGH: **MAD hits exactly 0 whenever a strict majority of intervals repeat** — far easier than the old σ's "every interval identical", and real cron produces bit-identical gaps by the dozen — which would have been a *worse* permanent blind spot than the code being replaced. A degenerate MAD now falls back to the mean absolute deviation scaled by `sqrt(pi/2)`; only a perfectly rigid history stays unquantifiable, so the documented metronome posture is untouched.

  **Every honest-unknown posture is preserved**: thin history (<5 firings) never flags, a rigid metronome is watched but unquantifiable, an untrusted or unscheduled window is watched but never flagged, and a failed cron-history read still skips that section and says so via `cron_skipped`. Flags now carry `expected_gap` (the rhythm the history implies); the legacy `ewma` key mirrors it so the shipped `signal-noise/cadence-flags` read-door envelope stays non-breaking, and the ability description states both. Read door unchanged at 37.

  [tests/ml-cadence.php](tests/ml-cadence.php) 15 → 33 asserts and [tests/ml-kernel.php](tests/ml-kernel.php) 96 → 110: the real poisoning shape (50 firings of ~1h gaps spanning two days against a 12h registration → must not flag) is pinned alongside a **non-vacuity assertion that the raw statistic on that exact series still z-scores over three** — what suppresses the flag is the new rule, not thin data. Every suppression test is paired with a negative control that changes one variable and re-admits the flag (the same 6.4h gap flags when registered hourly instead of twicedaily; the same clustered series flags once given a registration), a genuinely-stalled daily hook 3.5 days silent still flags, an hourly hook 6 hours silent still flags, and the exact boundaries (1.5× the interval, 0.5× on the agreement clause) are pinned on both sides.

## [10.31.0] - 2026-08-02

### Added

- **Desktop Mode AI-agent tool calls now feed the same `sn_tool_call` telemetry table as the MCP door — TWO seams, not one** ([inc/mcp/mcp-telemetry-agents.php](inc/mcp/mcp-telemetry-agents.php), door `agent`). Desktop Mode 0.9.8's agent runner never goes through `sn_mcp_call_tool()` — `includes/agents/runner.php:1190` calls `$ability->execute( $args )` directly — so every agent-driven tool call was invisible to `inc/mcp/mcp-telemetry.php`'s existing telemetry, a blind spot this closes without touching the MCP door itself.

  **Seam 1 — `desktop_mode_agent_tool_result` (`runner.php:575`)**: `apply_filters( 'desktop_mode_agent_tool_result', $output, $slug, $args, $agent_user_id )`, fired only on the success path (`! is_wp_error( $output )` gates the call itself at `runner.php:561-576`). **Adversarial review REJECTed the first cut on one HIGH**: seam 1 alone is structurally success-only, so `door='agent'` failure rate would have read as an artificial ~0% — this repo's standing "success-only readout" trap, recurring in a new place.

  **Seam 2 — `desktop_mode_agent_completed` (`runner.php:239`), added to close that HIGH**: `do_action( 'desktop_mode_agent_completed', $user_id, $message, $result, $context )` fires once per run, after both success AND failure. `$result['toolCalls']` (`runner.php:578-593`) carries one `{callId, name, args, output, error}` entry per tool call for the whole run; this seam inserts a row for every entry with a non-null `error`, skipping success entries (seam 1 already recorded those — a double-count guard test pins this) and any entry outside the namespace gate. Outcome is a flat, documented `server_error` for every seam-2 row — the WP_Error status/code that `sn_mcp_telemetry_classify_wp_error()` actually keys on does not survive into `toolCalls`, only the rendered message string does, and re-deriving a code from that message via substring matching is the regex-classifier mistake this program already killed once (session 2). **Residual, honestly-documented gap**: a run that dies before reaching the completed action at all (AI unavailable, rate limit, max-turns — `runner.php:216-224` returns early) still loses its tail of already-executed tool calls, because `$result` itself never reaches either seam in that case.

  **Reuses, never duplicates**: the row builder, insert, kill switch (`sn_mcp_telemetry_enabled`), WP_Error classifier, and `args_shape`/`args_hash`/`result_count` helpers all come straight from `inc/mcp/mcp-telemetry.php`; the slug→`tool_name` projection reuses `inc/mcp/mcp-tools.php`'s own `sn_mcp_tool_name_from_slug()` so the same ability reads identically whether it was called through the MCP door or an agent, on either seam.

  **Namespace filter, both directions, both seams**: only `signal-noise/*` (this plugin's own abilities) and `signal-and-noise/*` (the companion theme's, which this plugin's own `sn_site_facts` already dispatches directly) are recorded — everything else (`desktop-mode/get-post`, any other plugin) is silently ignored. The two prefixes are checked independently, not via a shared-prefix shortcut: this repo has hit the `strpos('signal-noise/')`-misses-`signal-and-noise/` bug before (they diverge at character 7).

  **Row shape**: `layer='server'` (inherited), `door='agent'` (new value, fits the existing `VARCHAR(8)` column), `actor='agent:<user_login>'` (falls back to `agent:#<id>` when unresolvable). **Deviation from the original brief**: `latency_ms` is stored as `0`, not `NULL`, on both seams — neither hook has a timing start point, and the `latency_ms INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` column can't hold NULL regardless; an honest zero beats a fabricated duration. See [docs/mcp-consolidation/FINDINGS.md](docs/mcp-consolidation/FINDINGS.md).

  **Fail-open identical to the MCP layer, both seams**: kill switch, try/catch around every recording step. Seam 1's filter callback unconditionally returns `$output` byte-identical in every case (success, WP_Error, and weird/unexpected shapes) — pinned by a deep-compare test across all three; seam 2's action callback has no return value to protect but is held to the same standard (malformed `$result`/`toolCalls`/entry shapes are silent per-entry no-ops, with a test asserting zero PHP warnings/notices across every malformed shape). Desktop Mode absent means neither hook ever fires: zero cost, and the require is positioned after `mcp-tools.php`/`mcp-telemetry.php` with `function_exists` guards so load order can never fatal.

  [tests/mcp-telemetry-agents.php](tests/mcp-telemetry-agents.php) — 58 non-vacuous asserts across both seams (up from 30 pre-review): the original seam-1 suite (passthrough deep-compare across success/WP_Error/weird-object/null/scalar, namespace filtering, actor resolution, outcome classification, row shape, kill switch, fail-open, wiring via `apply_filters()`) plus seam-2's failure-row shape, double-count guard (success entries insert nothing from the action path), mixed success+failure runs, namespace gate on failures, an exhaustive malformed-shape sweep (missing `toolCalls`, non-array `$result`, non-array entries, missing `name`/`error`/`args` keys) asserting both zero writes AND zero PHP warnings, kill switch, fail-open, and end-to-end wiring via a real `do_action()` call. Watched RED twice: removing the seam-1 implementation file fatals the whole suite before the fix restores it green; renaming the seam-2 callback to simulate its absence fatals only the seam-2 section, in exactly the section that names it, before restoring it green.

## [10.30.0] - 2026-08-02

### Added

- **`signal-noise/sn-validate` — the consolidated read-door validation tool (MCP consolidation session 5)** ([inc/abilities-sn-validate.php](inc/abilities-sn-validate.php), [inc/sn-validate-checks.php](inc/sn-validate-checks.php), [inc/sn-validate-checks-media.php](inc/sn-validate-checks-media.php)). Deterministic, model-free checking of PROPOSED content before it is ever written — the inversion of the `ai-*-suggest` layer documented in `~/.claude/session-data/SN-MCP-new/sn-validate-spec.md`: each generator's implicit rule becomes an explicit, callable check. Read door widens 36 → 37 (plugin-namespace 26 → 27).

  **Nine checkable surfaces**: `excerpt` (word/sentence count, via `inc/word-count.php`'s Unicode-safe counter), `meta_description` (hard char cap REUSED from `SNT_SURFACES_FIELD_CAPS['meta_description']`, soft window sourced from `SNT_AI_META_DESC_SYSTEM`'s prose, plus a corpus-wide `corpus_collision` check against `_sn_meta_description` postmeta), `og_card_title` (hard cap reused, soft window sourced from `SNT_AI_OG_CARD_TITLE_SYSTEM`, plus `title_divergence` from the post title), `note_summary` (single-sentence structural check + a word cap mirrored from the theme's `ai-generate-page-note-summary` input schema), `tags` (existing `post_tag` vocabulary membership only — mirrors `suggest-tags`' own constraint), `alt_text` (hard cap reused from `SNT_AI_ALT_APPLY_MAX_LENGTH`, soft window sourced from `SNT_AI_ALT_SUGGEST_SYSTEM`, filename-pattern rejection, and a redundant-prefix list extracted from `SNT_AI_ALT_BASE_RULES`), `links` (target exists + published, not self, not already linked — via the REUSED `sn_health_contains_note_link()` — anchor present in the source body), `body` (a `drift_lexicon` check that REUSES `sn_health_drift_time_patterns()` verbatim, and a `block_pattern_registered` check against WP core's `WP_Block_Patterns_Registry` for any `core/pattern` block referenced), and `brand_voice` (evidence-only: banned-phrase hits extracted from `SNT_AI_EXCERPT_SYSTEM`'s prose, sentence-length distribution, em-dash count — **never a score, never a verdict**, applied to whichever text surface is resolved).

  **Every limit is reused, none re-declared.** The anti-drift discipline the spec names as the tool's entire justification: hard character caps come from `SNT_SURFACES_FIELD_CAPS` and `SNT_AI_ALT_APPLY_MAX_LENGTH` at call time (never copied); the drift-phrase lexicon is `sn_health_drift_time_patterns()` itself, not a second pattern list; the "already linked" check is `sn_health_contains_note_link()` itself; tag vocabulary membership resolves through `sn_tag_normalize_key()`. Where no machine-readable constant existed (the soft length windows and banned-phrase list live only as prose inside the `ai-generate-*` system-instruction constants), the values were extracted ONCE with an inline citation of the exact constant they were read from — documented, not invented, and never duplicated a second time.

  **Severity model, exactly per spec**: `error` is an objective rule violation and blocks (`ready_to_apply:false`); `warning` is a heuristic signal that never blocks; `info` is evidence for a human judgment call (brand_voice, exclusively) and never blocks, never scores. `finding_id = sha256(surface|check|content-identity)` — the same content-derived scheme as `sn_scan`'s `candidate_id` — proven byte-identical across reruns of the same proposal.

  **`checks:"all"` with no proposal validates the post's PUBLISHED surfaces**, never errors on the absence of a proposal (only `excerpt`, `meta_description`, `og_card_title`, `body`, and `tags` have a natural published form this plugin stores; `note_summary`/`alt_text`/`links` are proposal-only and are silently skipped, not errored, when absent). `compare_against:"published"` (the default) attaches a simple per-surface `{published, proposed}` presence diff for every surface actually present in the proposal — deliberately not over-built into a semantic diff/patch (session-5 scope cut).

  **STATELESS + ZERO WRITES**, proven by a write-recorder guard in [tests/abilities-sn-validate.php](tests/abilities-sn-validate.php) (same pattern as `sn_scan`'s zero-writes guard, session 4) exercised across every check family. **ZERO MODEL CALLS**, pinned by a structural source scan (acceptance test 6) that strips comments via `token_get_all()` before checking for `wp_ai_client_prompt`, `snt_ai_generate_with_constraints`, and the `wp_remote_*` transport — a raw substring scan would have false-positived on this very file's own header, which documents the guarantee in prose.

  **Scope cut (session 5, recorded per the kickoff)**: `sn_apply` does not exist yet (sessions 6-7) — acceptance tests 2 and 3's "apply refuses/succeeds" halves are deferred; this session pins `ready_to_apply` SEMANTICS only (a known error yields `ready_to_apply:false`; warnings-only yields `true`), not an actual enforcement call.

  Read allowlist widened in [inc/mcp/mcp-capabilities.php](inc/mcp/mcp-capabilities.php); [tests/mcp-capabilities.php](tests/mcp-capabilities.php) pins updated (36 → 37 / 26 → 27 plugin). New standalone suite [tests/abilities-sn-validate.php](tests/abilities-sn-validate.php), 44 asserts: all six acceptance tests pinned explicitly (determinism, error/warning `ready_to_apply` semantics, a planted `corpus_collision` duplicate, `checks:"all"` against published surfaces, and the comment-stripped zero-model-call source scan), plus 4xx coverage per bad input, the zero-writes guard, and per-surface check coverage (alt_text/links/tags/body/note_summary/brand_voice/diff). Full deviation ledger in [docs/mcp-consolidation/FINDINGS.md](docs/mcp-consolidation/FINDINGS.md) (session-5 section).

## [10.29.0] - 2026-08-02

### Added

- **`signal-noise/sn-scan` — the consolidated read-door scan tool (MCP consolidation session 4)** ([inc/abilities-sn-scan.php](inc/abilities-sn-scan.php), [inc/sn-scan-adapters.php](inc/sn-scan-adapters.php)). Absorbs five existing scan abilities — `block-migrations-scan`, `pattern-adoption-scan`, `duplicate-body-scan`, `near-duplicate-scan`, `link-candidates` — behind one `scan_type` enum, plus a NEW sixth source, `orphan_media`, wrapping the pure-SQL `sn_health_check_orphaned_media()` detector (never the AI-gated `ai-orphan-suggest` path — this tool calls no model, ever). NEW ALONGSIDE OLD: all five absorbed abilities stay registered, untouched, unremoved; read door widens 35 → 36 (plugin-namespace 25 → 26).

  **Thin wrapper, not an ability-to-ability proxy.** Every adapter calls the SAME internal PHP compute the corresponding standalone ability calls (`snt_block_migrations_compute()`, `snt_pattern_adoption_compute()`, `snt_corpus_duplicate_scan()`, `snt_ml_cousin_pairs()`, `snt_ml_link_candidates()` fanned out per source post, `sn_health_check_orphaned_media()`) — never `wp_get_ability()` — so reshaping into the envelope costs no double-marshalling. Confirms FINDINGS.md #5's two-scan-family split: `block_migrations`/`pattern_adoption`/`duplicate_body`/`orphan_media` are pure structural detectors that never touch `inc/ml-kernel.php`; `near_duplicate`/`link_candidates` share the kernel's TF-IDF/cosine primitives.

  **Deterministic candidate IDs, the spec's non-negotiable core**: `candidate_id = sha256(scan_type + target_identity + content_fingerprint)`, hex, reusing each scan's own content-derived fingerprint (`block_fingerprint` = `md5(serialize_block(node))` for the two structural block scans; per-post `content_hash` for `duplicate_body`/`near_duplicate`; a source/target composite for `link_candidates`; `md5(subject_url)` for `orphan_media`) — never a per-run UUID. Ordering is always `confidence DESC, candidate_id ASC`; two runs against unchanged content return byte-identical `candidates` arrays, `corpus_fingerprint`, and `scan_run_id` (proven directly — acceptance test 1).

  **Confidence mapping**: `near_duplicate` uses the pipeline's own cosine directly (already `[0.3, 0.95]` by construction); `link_candidates` uses the ML related-index score, clamped `[0,1]`; the four sources with no native score use documented constants (`duplicate_body` 1.0 — exact hash match is certain; `block_migrations` 0.9 — a deterministic WCAG rule match; `orphan_media` 0.85 — the detector's own docblock calls itself "conservative by design"; `pattern_adoption` 0.7 — a stylistic opportunity, not a defect).

  **`freshness` reports what actually happened, not what was requested.** `block_migrations`/`pattern_adoption`/`duplicate_body`/`near_duplicate`/`orphan_media` always recompute live — none of their underlying detectors read from a cache, so `freshness` is always `"fresh"` regardless of the input. `link_candidates` reads the prebuilt `_snt_ml_related` artifact and can never honor `freshness:"fresh"` without a rebuild — and this tool writes nothing, ever — so it always reports `"cached"`. The `freshness` input is accepted (schema-valid values only) but does not change behavior.

  **`dismissed` is always `false` today.** `block_migrations`/`pattern_adoption`'s underlying detectors already filter dismissed candidates out of their own return value (the existing `dismiss-candidate` store) before this tool ever sees them; the other four sources have no dismissal store at all (`sn_dismiss` is a later consolidation phase, per FINDINGS.md #5). `include_dismissed` is accepted but inert everywhere — documented in the tool description, not silently swallowed.

  **`apply_hint` — wired only where the fingerprint genuinely validates.** `block_migrations` → `block-migrations-apply`, `pattern_adoption` → `pattern-adoption-apply` (both required `{post_id, block_fingerprint, replacement_markup, migration_type|pattern_type}` — proven end-to-end, scan → suggest → apply, never a 409, on a fixture post: acceptance test 5, the real gate). `orphan_media` → `ai-orphan-apply` (`{attachment_id}` only — no fingerprint gate exists to violate, so test 5 is vacuously satisfied). `duplicate_body`/`near_duplicate` → `null` (no apply path exists — a human resolves these manually). `link_candidates` → **deliberately `null`**, a deviation from the original task framing: `ai-link-apply` validates a POSITIONAL fingerprint (`snt_ai_drift_fingerprint()`, an anchor + raw-content offset) that only an AI-mediated suggest call (`ai-link-suggest`/`ai-pair-suggest`) can produce — this deterministic kernel scan has no anchor or position to offer. Wiring `apply_hint` here would fail acceptance test 5 by construction and would smuggle a model call one hop away from a tool whose contract is "writes nothing, ever calls no model." See FINDINGS.md session-4 for the full trace.

  Read allowlist widened in [inc/mcp/mcp-capabilities.php](inc/mcp/mcp-capabilities.php); [tests/mcp-capabilities.php](tests/mcp-capabilities.php) pins updated deliberately (35 → 36 / 25 → 26 plugin). New standalone integration suite [tests/abilities-sn-scan.php](tests/abilities-sn-scan.php), 76 asserts (later 92 after the adversarial-review fixes below): all five acceptance tests from the spec pinned explicitly (byte-identical reruns, dismiss-then-rescan, edit-then-rescan ID change, clean cursor paging with no dupes/gaps, and the scan→suggest→apply fingerprint-parity round trip for both structural apply paths), plus candidate_id derivation, ordering, and scope/cursor/freshness 4xx coverage. Full deviation ledger, the orphan-media non-AI-detector finding, and the two-scan-family cost note are in [docs/mcp-consolidation/FINDINGS.md](docs/mcp-consolidation/FINDINGS.md) (session-4 section).

### Fixed (same v10.29.0 ship, adversarial review before merge)

- **HIGH — `sn_scan` was writing despite declaring `readonly:true`.** `snt_block_migrations_run_scan()` and `snt_pattern_adoption_run_scan()` (`inc/block-migrations-detect.php`, `inc/pattern-adoption-detect.php`) each end with an unconditional `set_transient()` caching the per-user result for the admin tab — the `block_migrations`/`pattern_adoption` adapters called these directly, so every `sn_scan` call on those two types wrote the options table and clobbered the legacy per-user 1h cache the standalone ability and admin tab read. **Fix**: extracted the pure compute into new `snt_block_migrations_compute()` / `snt_pattern_adoption_compute()` (everything except the `set_transient()`); `run_scan()` is now `compute()` + the write, byte-identical for every existing caller (pinned by a new assertion that `run_scan()` still writes the same transient key with the same shape). The sn_scan adapters call `compute()` only. A new suite-level guard (`tests/abilities-sn-scan.php`) runs all 6 `scan_type`s through `snt_ability_sn_scan()` with a stub `$wpdb`/transient layer that RECORDS every write call and asserts zero across the board — this pins the read-only contract structurally, not per-adapter, so a future scan_type that starts writing fails the same guard automatically. Watched RED: the guard test failed with 2 recorded `set_transient()` calls against the pre-fix adapters (reproduced below), confirming the review's finding before the fix landed.
- **MEDIUM — `duplicate_body`'s `targets[]` member order was DB-order-dependent, not canonicalized.** `snt_corpus_duplicate_scan()` orders posts `post_date DESC` with no tie-break; two posts sharing a `post_date` (the bulk-import case this scan exists to catch) could return in either order across runs, so `targets[]` — though `target_identity` was already order-independent — was not guaranteed byte-identical. **Fix**: `snt_sn_scan_adapter_duplicate_body()` now `usort()`s each group's members by `post_id` ASC before assigning to `targets`. `near_duplicate`'s pair order was already guaranteed by `snt_ml_cousin_pairs()` itself (`a.post_id < b.post_id`) but the adapter now re-asserts it defensively rather than trusting the upstream invariant to hold forever; `link_candidates`' `[source, target]` order is semantic (not sortable) and was already order-independent of any unstable DB order — both audited, neither needed the `duplicate_body` fix. Acceptance test 1 (byte-identical reruns) extended to all six `scan_type`s, with a `duplicate_body` fixture whose stub deliberately returns two same-post_date duplicates in a DIFFERENT member order across the two runs — the canonicalization is what makes the assertion pass; watched RED against the pre-fix adapter confirmed the test would otherwise be vacuous (it failed without the `usort()`).
- **MEDIUM — a false "TOCTOU-checked" safety claim in `inc/sn-scan-adapters.php`'s `orphan_media` comment.** `ai-orphan-apply`'s pre-delete check (`inc/ai-orphan-suggest.php:172-198`) re-verifies capability and that the attachment still exists — it never re-verifies the attachment is STILL unreferenced at apply time. Comment corrected to state the gap plainly (pre-existing in `ai-orphan-apply`, not introduced by sn_scan); recorded in FINDINGS.md as input for the `sn_apply` gate design (sessions 6-7).

  Full sweep after these fixes: see FINDINGS.md session-4 for the exact counts.

## [10.28.1] - 2026-08-01

### Fixed

- **TOCTOU gap in the orphan-media force-delete closed** ([inc/ai-orphan-suggest.php](inc/ai-orphan-suggest.php)). `snt_ai_orphan_apply_impl()` checked only `current_user_can('delete_post')` + attachment existence before `wp_delete_attachment($id, true)` — it never re-verified that the attachment was still orphaned at apply time. Between the health scan that flagged it and the Apply click, the attachment could become referenced again (set as a featured image, inserted into a post body, made the site logo/icon, added to post meta) and would be permanently deleted anyway. The apply impl now re-runs the full scan-time signal battery via a new `sn_health_attachment_is_referenced_now()` before the irreversible delete; a now-referenced attachment returns `WP_Error snt_orphan_no_longer` (409) and nothing is deleted. The verdict transient is deliberately left in place so the finding stays reviewable after the refusal. Found during MCP consolidation session 4 review ([docs/mcp-consolidation/FINDINGS.md](docs/mcp-consolidation/FINDINGS.md)); this apply-time re-verify pattern also feeds the `sn_apply` gate design.

### Changed

- **Reference-set building extracted into `sn_health_reference_sets()`** ([inc/health-check-orphaned-media.php](inc/health-check-orphaned-media.php)): the featured-image + site-chrome flipped sets are now built by one shared helper consumed by both the scan and the new apply-time re-check — scan/apply parity is structural rather than copied. The `ai-orphan-apply` ability description now documents the 409 refusal.

### Testing

- New [tests/ai-orphan-apply.php](tests/ai-orphan-apply.php) (19 assertions, harness copied from the known-good `health-orphan-detection.php` substring-corpus wpdb sibling): pins all three race classes (post body, featured image, site logo) as 409-with-zero-`wp_delete_attachment`-calls, the still-orphan happy path as exactly one `(id, true)` delete call, and the pre-existing 403/422/500 gates as unchanged — including the real WP 7.0 `wp_delete_attachment` failure shape (`false`, never an array). Watched RED first: 10 failures reproducing the race (deletes proceeded on referenced attachments), then green.

## [10.28.0] - 2026-08-01

### Fixed

- **All eight Desktop Mode widgets blocked the desktop theme's typeface** ([assets/desktop-mode-widget*.js](assets/)). desktop-mode 0.9.7 added **desktop themes** — an uploadable ZIP that reskins the whole shell, including its typography. The shell delivers a themed face by setting `font-family: var( --desktop-mode-font, inherit )` on the shell root and letting it **inherit**; its own comment in `assets/css/desktop.css` names the consumers as "dock labels, desktop icon labels, WIDGETS, the overview" (verified at tag v0.9.8). Every SN widget declared its own `-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, …` stack — 15 declarations across 8 files — each of which silently won over the inherited value. A user who installed a themed font saw it everywhere on the desktop except our widgets. All local typefaces removed; `font-size`, `line-height` and `font-weight` are untouched, and Quick Actions' `font:` shorthand (which resets the family as surely as `font-family` does) became explicit longhands.

### Changed

- **Colour literals in the widgets deliberately NOT migrated to the `--wpd-*` palette**, with the reasoning recorded in [assets/desktop-mode-widget-actions.js](assets/desktop-mode-widget-actions.js). Adopting the theme palette looks like the obvious companion change and is the wrong call here: `.desktop-mode-widgets__card` is still `background-color: rgba( 20, 20, 22, 0.55 )` at v0.9.8 — a **literal**, the one surface a desktop theme cannot retint — while `--wpd-success-fg` and friends are themed to read against `--wpd-surface`, which *is* themeable. Under a light theme those tokens resolve dark, so the swap would have put dark green and dark amber on permanently dark glass: a contrast **regression** dressed as theme support. A fixed surface takes a fixed foreground. Two further findings recorded in the same note: `--wpd-color-*` (the tokens desktop-mode's own `widget-starter.css` instructs widget authors to use, claiming the shell sets them) is still assigned nowhere at v0.9.8 — first-party widgets disagree on the fallback, near-black vs near-white, which is only possible if the variable never resolves; and the card's `color` *has* become themeable (`var( --wpd-fg-on-accent, #fff )`), an upstream coupling that hits desktop-mode's own widgets identically and is tracked rather than diverged from.

### Testing

- New section in [tests/desktop-mode-integration.php](tests/desktop-mode-integration.php) pins the property — *no SN widget declares a typeface* — rather than any wording: one assertion per widget for `font-family`, plus a shorthand check that allows `font:inherit` and rejects any other `font:` value. Watched **RED first** (9 failures naming all eight widgets and the shorthand), then green. Also closed a coverage hole found while writing it: `desktop-mode-widget-anchors.js` was missing from the `$sn_widget_js` map entirely, so the light-palette and doubled-heading assertions had never run against it. Suite 282 → 300 assertions, 0 failed.

- **Site Health false alarm: the on-demand analytics warmer read as "NOT scheduled"** ([inc/cron-dashboard.php](inc/cron-dashboard.php)). `sn_analytics_rollup` is the SWR warmer's SINGLE-event hook — it schedules via `wp_schedule_single_event()` and clears after every firing, so "unscheduled" is its documented resting state between admin visits (the two-hook design comment in [inc/analytics-rollup.php](inc/analytics-rollup.php); the recurring schedule lives on `sn_analytics_rollup_daily`, which was healthy the whole time). The Site Health classifier's `snt_cron_hook_is_expected()` gate only exempted the two config-gated hooks (insights scan, uptime heartbeat), so the warmer's normal resting state raised a permanent "1 recommended improvement" — the exact "unscheduled BY DESIGN must not read as a pipeline issue" noise rule (v8.1.2) applied to a third hook class. New `snt_cron_hook_is_on_demand()` marks the warmer: its panel line now reads `on-demand (single events, clears after firing)` instead of the alarming `NOT scheduled`, it never joins the issues list, and it's exempt from the >2× interval staleness math (its firing cadence tracks admin visits, not cron health — and live single events carry no schedule slug anyway). The actual rollup pipeline was never broken; this fixes the readout, not the cron.

Tests 9/9b in [tests/cron-site-health.php](tests/cron-site-health.php) now pin the resting state (unscheduled + last-fired 16h ago → `good`, labeled on-demand) and the staleness exemption; watched RED against the pre-fix classifier (4 failures reproducing the live screenshot), then green. ## [10.27.0] - 2026-07-31

### Added

Shape: `[{surface, hits}, ...]`, descending by hits, an empty array (never omitted) when no AI-training family read anything in the window.

The ability's `output_schema` gains the matching `{surface, hits}` item schema and its description names the new field. The Desktop Mode tile renders a sub-row per surface under "Declared AI-training", guarded on presence (`payload.ai_surfaces && payload.ai_surfaces.length`) so an older cached payload renders exactly as before.

Full suite green (`tests/*.php` minus `contracts-smoke.php`), `php -l`, `composer phpstan` (no errors), `phpcs` clean on touched files.

### Added

- **`sn_posts` and `sn_site_facts` — the first two CONSOLIDATED MCP tools** ([inc/abilities-sn-posts.php](inc/abilities-sn-posts.php), [inc/abilities-sn-site-facts.php](inc/abilities-sn-site-facts.php), registered `signal-noise/sn-posts` / `signal-noise/sn-site-facts`; read door 33 → 35): session 3 of the MCP consolidation program (`~/.claude/session-data/SN-MCP-new/sn-mcp-consolidation.md`, phase 2 — "lowest risk, immediate quality-of-life"). NEW ALONGSIDE OLD: every absorbed ability (`list-posts`, `get-post-content`, and 9 of 11 `sn_site_facts` sources) stays registered and doored, untouched.

  **`sn_posts`** absorbs `list-posts` + `get-post-content`: content is an opt-in FIELD (`include_content: bool`), not a different return shape. `scope` selects the target set — `{kind:"all"}` (default), `{kind:"post_ids", post_ids:[...]}`, `{kind:"modified_since", modified_since:"..."}`, or `{kind:"post_type", post_type:"..."}` — all reusing [inc/corpus-inspect.php](inc/corpus-inspect.php)'s existing query/row primitives verbatim (`snt_corpus_fetch_posts`, `snt_corpus_post_row`, `snt_corpus_post_type_allowed`, `snt_corpus_post_type_error`), not re-implemented. `include_content:true` is HARD-capped at 20 posts and **rejects (422) rather than truncates** when the resolved scope exceeds it — mirrors `update-post-surfaces`' reject-never-truncate posture, and applies to the scope's full resolved count so it can't be bypassed by paginating around it. Cursor-paginated (opaque `base64(offset)` — the spec names no concrete encoding, so this is a deviation-by-necessity); `post_ids` scope returns its bounded set unpaginated, exactly like the old `get-post-content`. Deterministic ordering throughout (date/modified DESC + ID DESC tie-break, never database order).

  **`sn_site_facts`** absorbs 10 of the 11 named sources (`get-design-system-summary` is RETIRED, not absorbed, per the spec — its own description says it's an AI-prompt formatting layer the raw `design_tokens` fact supersedes). 9 of the 10 sources are THEME abilities (`signal-and-noise/*`); this plugin never re-implements their logic, it dispatches `wp_get_ability(<source>)->check_permissions()` then `->execute()` — the same sequence `sn_mcp_call_tool()` itself uses. Per-fact graceful degradation: a theme-absent site, an unregistered/retired source, a permission denial, or an execute() failure collapses THAT fact's map entry to `{error:"unavailable"}` while every other requested fact still returns — the call as a whole only errors on invalid input (unknown fact name, empty `facts[]`, or a missing `slug` when `reading_time`, `seo_route_meta`, or `active_template` is requested — 400, not 422, per spec). Fact→source map: `theme_version`→`get-theme-version`, `latest_theme_tag`→`get-latest-theme-tag`, `design_tokens`→`get-design-tokens`, `block_patterns`→`list-block-patterns`, `template_overrides`→`list-template-overrides` (plugin-namespace, not theme), `active_template`→`get-active-template-structure`, `llms_txt`→`get-llms-txt`, `seo_route_meta`→`get-seo-route-meta`, `pillars`→`get-page-notes-pillars`, `reading_time`→`get-reading-time-for-slug`.

  **`active_template` requires `slug` (adversarial review round 2, fixed before this entry shipped).** The first cut dispatched `active_template` with no args, reading its `anyOf(post_id, slug)` source schema as fully optional. Verified against the theme's real source (`signal-and-noise` repo, `inc/abilities-diagnostics.php:535-554`): with neither argument, the execute callback deterministically returns a 404 `WP_Error` — there is no no-args default path — so every `active_template` call was silently degrading to `{error:"unavailable"}` forever, on a healthy site. `active_template` now joins `reading_time`/`seo_route_meta` in the slug-required set, dispatched with the same `{slug: ...}` shape. Full account in [docs/mcp-consolidation/FINDINGS.md](docs/mcp-consolidation/FINDINGS.md).

  **Naming deviation** (both tools): the spec writes bare `sn_posts`/`sn_site_facts`, but this server derives MCP tool names from ability SLUGS via `sn_mcp_tool_name_from_slug()` — registered as `signal-noise/sn-posts` / `signal-noise/sn-site-facts` (→ MCP tool names `signal-noise__sn-posts` / `signal-noise__sn-site-facts`) rather than special-casing the name mapper for two slugs. Every `new WP_Error(...)` this session carries `array('status'=>N)`, so both tools' error rows classify correctly through the v10.25.0 Layer B telemetry status-first scheme with zero special-casing — pinned directly in [tests/abilities-sn-posts.php](tests/abilities-sn-posts.php) (a real `sn-posts` schema violation run through the actual `sn_mcp_telemetry_classify_wp_error()`).

  Tests: [tests/abilities-sn-posts.php](tests/abilities-sn-posts.php) (45 asserts) + [tests/abilities-sn-site-facts.php](tests/abilities-sn-site-facts.php) (38 asserts, up from 31 — the `active_template` fix added missing-slug coverage, a theme-contract-faithful stub that 404s on empty args, and a standing dispatcher-level regression guard), both watched RED against deliberately reintroduced bugs before each fix — genuine failures confirmed, then restored green. [tests/mcp-capabilities.php](tests/mcp-capabilities.php)'s pinned allowlist counts updated deliberately (33→35 total, 23→25 plugin-namespace, 10 theme unchanged).

> **Why MINOR:** two new user-visible, additive MCP tools; nothing absorbed is removed, unregistered, or behaviorally changed, and the read door's existing 33 tools respond byte-identically.

## [10.25.0] - 2026-07-31

### Added

- **MCP Layer B telemetry** ([inc/mcp/mcp-telemetry.php](inc/mcp/mcp-telemetry.php), new module): every `tools/call` through `sn_mcp_call_tool()` — both doors, every outcome — now writes one row to a new dormant table `{$wpdb->prefix}sn_tool_call` (created lazily on `init`, same version-guarded dbDelta idiom as [inc/analytics-buckets.php](inc/analytics-buckets.php)). This is the "server middleware" half of the two-layer telemetry design (`~/.claude/session-data/SN-MCP-new/sn-telemetry-spec.md`); the client-side Claude Code hook half shipped separately and already writes to `~/.claude/telemetry/mcp-calls.jsonl`. Columns: `ts` (UTC, millisecond precision via `microtime()` — never `UNIX_TIMESTAMP`/session-tz), `layer` (`server`, fixed this session), `door` (`read`|`rw`), `actor` (`human` or `app-pw:<8-char UUID prefix>` today — `routine:<name>` is reserved, no code path produces it yet — resolved via the existing rw-audit app-password resolver, reused for both doors since it is door-agnostic), `tool_name`, `args_shape` (sorted top-level keys only), `args_hash` (sha256 of the JSON-encoded arguments — never a raw value, and never the spec's original reversible base64 prefix per session 1's corrected deviation), `outcome` (`ok`|`schema_error`|`not_found`|`refused`|`server_error`), `refusal_gate` (`rate_limit`|`write_throttle`|`permission`, nullable), `latency_ms`, `result_count` (only for a trivially list-shaped top-level result, else NULL), `candidate_id` (reserved, always NULL this session).

  Outcome classification is **status-first**, grounded against a paren-balanced sweep of every `new WP_Error(` construction under `inc/` (196 total — a plain single-line `grep` undercounts badly, since most multi-line constructions are invisible to it): 168 carry `array('status'=>N)`, mapped by band (429 → `refused`; 400–428/431–499 → `schema_error`; ≥500 → `server_error`); of the 28 status-less constructions, a reachability check (does any ability's `execute()` propagate it raw?) found exactly one that is: `sn_tag_not_unused` (`inc/tag-consolidation.php`, reached via `signal-noise/prune-unused-tags`) → `schema_error`; everything else status-less defaults to `server_error` (an unexplained failure isn't proven the caller's fault). `snt_surfaces_throttled` (a per-post write-cap, the only status-429 construction found) gets its own `refusal_gate: 'write_throttle'` rather than being lumped in with the rw door's rate-limit gate. An earlier version of this classifier used a code-name regex (`invalid|unknown|missing|not_found`) grounded on a single-line grep that missed every multi-line construction and mis-scored six real codes (including flagging `snt_impl_missing`, a genuine HTTP-500 dependency failure, as a schema error on the `missing` substring) — caught by adversarial review before merge, replaced with the status-first scheme above. Because the WP_Error's status DATA (not just its message) is required, the interception point is inside `sn_mcp_call_tool()` itself, at the same tail positions `inc/mcp/mcp-rw-audit.php` already uses — NOT `inc/mcp/mcp-server.php`'s `tools/call` case as originally scoped, since by that point an execute() failure has already been flattened to a message-only string.

  Fully fail-open (a missing table, a failed `$wpdb->insert()`, or any exception is a silent no-op — the tool's own response is byte-identical either way, pinned in [tests/mcp-telemetry.php](tests/mcp-telemetry.php)), respects a `sn_mcp_telemetry_enabled` filter (default true), and prunes itself opportunistically (~1-in-50 inserts run a capped `DELETE ... LIMIT 500` for rows past the 90-day retention window, via `wp_rand()` — no cron, per the standing "schedule nothing" guardrail). [tests/mcp-telemetry.php](tests/mcp-telemetry.php): asserts include that no argument VALUE ever reaches the inserted row, that a forced `wpdb->insert()` failure never surfaces to the caller, and the full status-band classification matrix (400/422/429/500/status-less-known/status-less-unknown).

> **Why MINOR:** a new, additive, zero-tool, fail-open observability surface — no schema change to anything existing, no user action required, and both MCP doors keep responding byte-identically whether telemetry succeeds, fails, or is switched off.

## [10.24.0] - 2026-07-30

### Fixed

- **Unicode-safe word counting everywhere** ([inc/word-count.php](inc/word-count.php), new pure module): `str_word_count` is ASCII-only — accented letters split words apart and standalone numbers count as ZERO, so schema.org `wordCount` published wrong numbers for digit-bearing prose and reading times under-counted. `snt_word_count()` (any run of Unicode letters/numbers — what a reader counts) replaces it at all four sites: reading time, schema `wordCount`, the AI-prepop gate, AI excerpt length. Own tiny module so CLI fixtures load exactly it (13 asserts in [tests/word-count.php](tests/word-count.php), incl. interior-apostrophe/hyphen PARITY with the old counter — kept deliberately so reading times don't shift — and the invalid-UTF-8 never-zero guard); consumer fixtures gained the real dependency.

- **The dead reading-time redirect tier** ([inc/admin-legacy-redirect.php](inc/admin-legacy-redirect.php)): the cleanup tool retired in v10.0.0, but three legacy-map rows still routed to its ghost `content/reading-time` sub (the dispatcher silently fell back). Old bookmarks now land on the Content tab default, honestly labeled; the desktop-mode nav pin updated to the real destination.

- **Four stale/false claims retired**: [inc/analytics-recommendations.php](inc/analytics-recommendations.php)'s "O(n²) TF-IDF pass" description of unlinked_mentions (it is and always was an exact-title stripos sweep — the claim would mislead the next kernel audit); [inc/command-palette.php](inc/command-palette.php)'s docblock still selling the `signal-noise/v1/cmd/*` REST routes removed in v7.0.0 (the code migrated to `sntAbilityRun` correctly — only the story was stale); [inc/admin-page.php](inc/admin-page.php) + [inc/reading-time.php](inc/reading-time.php) naming the retired `sn_admin_reading_time_tab` hook as live; [docs/analytics-integrity-design.md](docs/analytics-integrity-design.md)'s "deploy-widget fix — separate PR" open item (CLOSED in v9.63.3; the doc now records the closure).

### Added

- **Kernel cadence verdicts ride the insights signal bundle** ([inc/insights.php](inc/insights.php)): the AI advisor's prompt now carries `cadence_flags` — subject + 2dp z from `snt_ml_cadence_flags()` — so it reasons about measured surprise instead of re-deriving staleness from raw minutes in-model. Additive and guarded; the raw `cron_freshness` rows are untouched (insights 214 → 219 asserts).

> **Why MINOR:** first batch of the 2026-07-30 aging-surface audit — a real fix with observable output changes (word counts), retired dead surfaces, and one additive signal. All items ranked one-liner tier; the audit's larger batches (BM25 consumer, cron-staleness re-base, migrations/IA-tier retirements) follow separately.

## [10.22.1] - 2026-07-30

### Fixed

- **Cron-freshness signal: session-timezone shift in `last_fired_ago_minutes`** ([inc/insights.php](inc/insights.php)): the insights signal collector read `snt_cron_history.fired_at` via SQL `UNIX_TIMESTAMP(fired_at)`, but the column stores UTC strings (cron-history writes `gmdate`) while MySQL's `UNIX_TIMESTAMP()` interprets its argument in the SESSION timezone — any non-UTC session silently shifted `last_fired_ago_minutes` (and the 24h-count cutoff) by the session offset. Now selects the raw `MAX(fired_at)` string and converts PHP-side with `strtotime($s . ' UTC')` — the established `snt_cron_history_for_hook()` idiom — and binds the 24h cutoff as a UTC datetime string so it compares in the column's own representation. The empty string is guarded BEFORE appending `' UTC'` (a lone `strtotime(' UTC')` resolves to the current time — the schedule-block trap). Tests: the fixture now models the real DB shape (raw UTC strings, numeric-string counts) and asserts under a UTC-3 PHP default timezone, plus a query-shape pin that no `UNIX_TIMESTAMP` reappears (Tests 7/7b, insights 209 → 214 asserts). Flagged MEDIUM/pre-existing by the v10.22.0 adversarial review.

> **Why PATCH:** a correctness fix to an existing signal; no new capability, no schema or API change.

## [10.17.0] - 2026-07-30

### New

- **Keyword + link candidates — ML pipeline #3** ([inc/ml-candidates.php](inc/ml-candidates.php)): two deterministic candidate generators for the human-in-the-loop editing workflow — the kernel proposes, the AI drafts elsewhere, a person decides; nothing here writes. `snt_ml_keyword_candidates( $post_id, $limit = 8 )` ranks the post's own terms by L2-normalized TF-IDF against corpus statistics built over ALL five non-trash statuses (the cousin-scan walk — rarity is judged against everything that could go live), unigrams plus adjacency BIGRAMS ("music provenance"): adjacent pairs in the raw word stream where BOTH members survive tokenization (a stopword between two survivors breaks adjacency — no fabricated bridging), scored as the pair's summed tf-idf × 1.25, competing in one weight-descending list (4dp, limit clamped 1..20). `snt_ml_link_candidates( $post_id, $limit = 5 )` reads the prebuilt related index (`_snt_ml_related` via `snt_ml_related_for_post`, 503 `snt_ml_not_built` while unbuilt — the related pipeline's exact contract) and subtracts every target the body ALREADY links to (internal /notes/ hrefs via `snt_ml_extract_note_links` — the same extractor the artifact build uses) plus every non-published target, fetching the full stored depth first so an exclusion opens a slot instead of shortening the answer; returns `{post_id, title, slug, score}` rows, limit clamped 1..10. Both hold the zero-vs-null line: unknown/trash/non-post ID → `snt_ml_no_post` (404); an EMPTY body → ok + zero candidates (an empty body is an ANSWER). Registered in the pipeline registry as `extract-keywords` and `link-candidates` ([inc/ml-pipelines.php](inc/ml-pipelines.php)) with the related pipeline's post_id gate (missing/non-positive → 400).

Input type is plain `'object'` because `post_id` is REQUIRED — the `[object,null]` union is reserved for no-required-fields abilities (the exact rule tests/abilities-categories.php Group E enforces). Allowlisted on the sn read door 29 → 31 (21 plugin + 10 theme; [inc/mcp/mcp-capabilities.php](inc/mcp/mcp-capabilities.php)), both pinned counts updated with dated assert text in [tests/mcp-capabilities.php](tests/mcp-capabilities.php). 65 asserts in [tests/ml-candidates.php](tests/ml-candidates.php): every keyword weight is a HAND-DERIVED 4dp constant worked from the formula independently of the kernel (incl. the bigram boost arithmetic, with the corpus-aware idf separation pinned — equal-tf terms rank by rarity), the members-must-survive/no-bridging bigram rule, both limit clamps at both bounds, 404-vs-empty-body, the already-linked exclusion pinned via a fixture body carrying a real /notes/ href that outranks every survivor, unpublished-target exclusion, the not-built 503 asserted against get_option's real absent shape BEFORE the stamp, and ability registration + wrapper delegation.

## [10.16.0] - 2026-07-30

### New

- **Near-duplicate COUSIN detection — ML pipeline #2** ([inc/ml-cousins.php](inc/ml-cousins.php)): the exact scan (`duplicate-body-scan`) catches byte-identical bodies only — a duplicated-then-lightly-edited post escapes it. `snt_ml_cousin_pairs( $threshold = 0.6 )` walks the FULL 'post' corpus (all five non-trash statuses via `snt_corpus_fetch_posts` — pre-publish collision checking is the point), tokenizes every body with the kernel, vectors them as L2-normalized TF-IDF against the corpus' own stats, and returns all pairs at/above the cosine threshold (clamped 0.3..0.95) — EXCLUDING byte-exact pairs (same `snt_corpus_content_hash`: those are the exact scan's finding, not a cousin), empty/whitespace-only bodies, and markup-only tokenless bodies. Each pair: `{ a: {post_id,title,slug,status}, b: {same}, cosine: 4dp }`, a = lower post_id, sorted cosine-descending. Computed on demand, NO caching — 34 posts is milliseconds, and fix-then-rescan honesty is the same reason the exact scan has none. Registered in the pipeline registry as `near-duplicates` next to `related` ([inc/ml-pipelines.php](inc/ml-pipelines.php)), whose wrapper accepts `{threshold}` and refuses to (float)-cast garbage (non-numeric → default, never a silent 0.0-clamped-to-0.3 widening).

- **New READ-door ability `signal-noise/near-duplicate-scan`** ([inc/abilities-corpus.php](inc/abilities-corpus.php)): fourth sibling of the corpus trio — manage_options, category tools, readonly/idempotent annotations, `[object, null]` input type per the bodyless-GET contract, input `{threshold: number 0.3..0.95 default 0.6}` (no post_type this release), output `{ok, pairs, pair_count, threshold, posts_scanned, truncated, scanned_at}`. The ability routes through `snt_ml_run()` — the registry stays the single ML dispatch seam. Allowlisted on the sn read door 28 → 29 (19 plugin + 10 theme; [inc/mcp/mcp-capabilities.php](inc/mcp/mcp-capabilities.php)), pinned counts updated in [tests/mcp-capabilities.php](tests/mcp-capabilities.php). 44 asserts in [tests/ml-cousins.php](tests/ml-cousins.php): the cosine pin is HAND-DERIVED (a permuted token multiset ⇒ cosine ≡ 1.0 whatever the idf — never recomputed from the kernel, the echo-testing ban), the excluded byte-exact pair also has cosine 1.0 so its absence proves the hash exclusion, the origin scheduled-vs-published cousin is asserted cross-status, and threshold clamping is pinned at both bounds with exact pair counts.

> **Why MINOR:** new user-visible capability (a second ML pipeline + a new read-door MCP tool); additive, zero new services, theme untouched.

## [10.15.0] - 2026-07-30

### New

- **The SN ML kernel — pure corpus intelligence** ([inc/ml-kernel.php](inc/ml-kernel.php)): the site grows its own relatedness math as a PURE module (zero WP calls, the inc/analytics-derive.php model — the fixture grep-pins the file free of WP function names): deterministic unicode tokenizer (Gutenberg block-comment + tag stripping, 46-word stopword list), smoothed-IDF corpus stats, sparse L2-normalized TF-IDF, sparse-safe cosine, Okapi BM25 (k1=1.2, b=0.75), Jaccard graph signals (tag overlap, direction-agnostic direct link, co-link), and the blended `snt_ml_related_score()` (.55 lexical / .25 tags / .15 direct link / .05 co-link, weights as a plain argument — the pure layer never filters). 70 asserts in [tests/ml-kernel.php](tests/ml-kernel.php), including a set_error_handler that fails the suite on ANY notice.

- **Pipeline registry** ([inc/ml-pipelines.php](inc/ml-pipelines.php)): a filterable slug=>callable map (`snt_ml_pipelines`) + one dispatcher `snt_ml_run()` (unknown slug → `snt_ml_unknown_pipeline`, 404-shaped), shipping the `related` pipeline whose docblock pins the artifact contract: `[]` is a real "nothing related" ANSWER, `null` means "artifacts not built" (→ `snt_ml_not_built`, 503-shaped) — zero and null are different answers, in both directions.

- **The artifact layer** ([inc/ml-artifacts.php](inc/ml-artifacts.php)): `snt_ml_build_corpus()` walks the published posts through the existing corpus walk (`snt_corpus_fetch_posts`), tokenizes bodies, extracts internal /notes/ links and tags as graph inputs, scores ALL pairs with the kernel (weights filterable HERE via `snt_ml_related_weights`), and stores each post's top 10 positive-score matches in `_snt_ml_related` meta (4dp) plus a corpus fingerprint + built_at in `snt_ml_corpus_meta` — never silent: an empty corpus returns ok:true/posts:0 and still stamps the option ("built over nothing" ≠ "never built"). The reader `snt_ml_related_for_post()` implements the pipeline contract verbatim and re-gates every row on publish status at READ time, so an unpublished post vanishes from every list before any rebuild. Rebuilds: transition into/out of publish (posts only, revision/autosave-guarded) coalesced through a deduped single event, plus a daily recurring backstop on a deliberately SEPARATE hook (the analytics-rollup shared-hook lesson).

- **Related notes on every note** ([inc/ml-related-render.php](inc/ml-related-render.php), [assets/ml-related-front.css](assets/ml-related-front.css)): a server-rendered `<aside class="snt-ml-related">` (mono kicker + up to 4 hard-framed links) appended via `the_content` @20, ONLY on singular main-query post views. Zero reader-facing JavaScript; stylesheet enqueues render-time only, brutalist idiom derived from maturity-index-front.css (hard borders, currentColor). Unbuilt artifacts and empty answers alike render NOTHING — build state is an admin concern, never a reader-visible error. 52 asserts in [tests/ml-artifacts.php](tests/ml-artifacts.php) model the real failure shapes: unbuilt (null), post unpublished since build, empty corpus, malformed meta rows, and core's `''`-for-absent-meta transform.

> **Why MINOR:** new user-visible capability (the Related notes section) + new internal ML surface; additive, zero new REST routes, zero new services, theme untouched.

## [10.6.1] - 2026-07-29

### Fixed

- **The voice fix: all three AI generator prompts rewritten** — the excerpt generator's output read as machine-written (5 of 7 scheduled notes carried "This piece" + verb), and the root cause was the prompt itself, not model drift: "Hook-driven — capture the reason a reader would click" instructs the model to describe the note from outside, which is exactly the register that shipped. Per-surface changes:
  - **Excerpt** ([inc/ai-excerpt.php](inc/ai-excerpt.php)): the excerpt is now specified as the *opening of the argument*, not a summary of it — same voice as the body, no reference to the note as an object, no advertising its contents, 50-75 words / 2-3 sentences / no sentence over 35 words, end on the claim. The register is anchored by a verbatim example (the owner's approved target for *Provenance signs the claim, not the truth*), and the banned list (em dashes, tricolons, repeated sentence openers, "not just X, but Y", hedge stacking, register tells) is the final check rather than the primary mechanism — a blocklist alone relocates the tell. The concise prepop variant now aliases the default (one register spec, two prompts drift); its token cap rises 120 → 160 so a 75-word excerpt is never clipped mid-sentence.
  - **Meta description** ([inc/ai-meta-description.php](inc/ai-meta-description.php)): written for the results-page reader with no context beyond the title — states what is true, never what the note "will do" for the reader; 140-160 hard, finished sentence at 160. Two context lines the prompt keys off are now threaded by the impl: an optional **`focus_keyword`** ability input (new, additive — the plugin stores no focus keyword, so a caller that knows it passes it; absent, the prompt falls back to the title's topic noun) and the post's **existing excerpt** (an instruction not to open like the excerpt is unfollowable against text the model has never seen). Concise truncation backstop raised 155 → 160 to stop trimming a finished 158-char sentence mid-clause.
  - **OG card title** ([inc/ai-og-card-title.php](inc/ai-og-card-title.php)): "punchier" (the clickbait pull, unopposed) replaced with the house rules by name — declarative restatement of the title's claim, no questions/curiosity gaps/numbered framing, no colon-as-hook, never a claim the note doesn't make nor a softened one it does, keep "provenance" when the title carries it, "proof of origin" never appears on this surface.
  - Regenerated against the new spec: all three surfaces for the seven scheduled notes (*Provenance signs the claim, not the truth* first — publishes 2026-07-31; *The pen is not the notary* keeps its corrected argument with only banned-list fixes; *Trust doesn't disappear, it relocates* regenerated for consistency with keep-if-not-better). Outputs applied via the editor after owner review — published notes untouched pending the owner's separate decision.

> **Why PATCH:** prompt calibration + a fix to the truncation backstop; the `focus_keyword` input is additive and optional; no schema migration, no removed API.

## [10.6.0] - 2026-07-29

### New

- **Corpus inspection: three read-only MCP tools on the sn read door** ([inc/corpus-inspect.php](inc/corpus-inspect.php), [inc/abilities-corpus.php](inc/abilities-corpus.php)): born from a live near-miss — a scheduled post carrying a different post's body verbatim (duplicate-to-seed, content never replaced), found two days before publish only by pasting bodies into claude.ai by hand. `signal-noise/duplicate-body-scan` hashes `md5(trim(post_content))` for every post across **all five non-trash statuses** (publish, future, draft, pending, private — pre-publish collision checking is the point) and returns groups where the same non-empty hash repeats, each member carrying ID/title/slug/status/date. Exact duplicates only, by design: raw hashing catches the duplicated-and-never-touched case; empty bodies never group (two blank drafts are not duplicates); the trim absorbs trailing-whitespace drift without drifting into near-match territory. `signal-noise/list-posts` is the metadata-only corpus listing (ID, title, slug, status, type, dates, categories, tags, word count, content hash, excerpt — manual excerpt else a 55-word strip-and-trim; **never a body**), because most collision checks resolve on title+tags+excerpt. `signal-noise/get-post-content` returns full bodies for a bounded 1-20 ID set, with unknown/trash/internal IDs reported in `missing` rather than silently dropped. Hardening throughout: all three gate on `manage_options` like the sibling scans (double-gated with the read door's own auth); a public-post-type gate keeps internal types (revisions would multiply every body into false duplicates) unwalkable even by an admin; the 2000-post query bound surfaces as an explicit `truncated` flag, never a silent cap; **no transients** — unlike the parse-heavy sibling scans these only hash strings, and the fix-then-rescan workflow makes a 1-hour stale cache a false alarm generator. Read door widens 25 → 28 (the rw door and `wp/v2` are untouched — the mutation surface does not grow). New fixture [tests/abilities-corpus.php](tests/abilities-corpus.php) (59 asserts) pins the hash primitive, cross-status grouping, the empty-body and internal-type exclusions, the missing-ID honesty, both caps, and the registration contract.

> **Why MINOR:** new user-visible capability (three abilities + three read-door MCP tools); no API change, no schema migration.

## [10.4.1] - 2026-07-29

### Fixed

- **`purge-all-caches` no longer claims "All caches purged." when its Cloudflare leg silently no-oped** ([inc/abilities-system.php](inc/abilities-system.php)): born from the 2026-07-29 resume-session incident — the CF PoP served stale CSS/HTML through multiple "successful" ability purges until a manual dashboard Purge Everything. The ability's filter dispatch never passed `verified => true`, so the theme's CF leg ran fire-and-forget `sn_cf_purge_everything()`: a silent `false` when no token/zone is configured, and a non-blocking POST whose response is never read when one is — the ability could not know whether CF purged anything, and asserted that it had. The dispatch now rides the verified path (the wp-admin "Purge All Caches" route since v8.7.0: blocking accept-confirmation + the theme's per-leg `sn_last_purge_report`), and the response carries an honest `cloudflare` verdict read back from that report: `confirmed` (CF answered `{success:true}`; `edge_fresh` surfaces the theme's post-purge route probes when present, with a stale-render warning in the message), `failed` (CF rejected the purge — `ok:false`, HTTP code in the message), `not_configured` (the purge never ran — `ok:false`, the message says why instead of claiming success), or `unconfirmed` (older theme wrote no verified report — dispatched, honestly unclaimed). A stale or auto-mode report never confirms a purge. The `count` field is unchanged — it counts template overrides cleared, which is why every incident response read `count:0` regardless of the CF leg. New fixture [tests/abilities-purge-cf-fail-loud.php](tests/abilities-purge-cf-fail-loud.php) pins all four verdicts, the verified dispatch flag, and the stale/auto-report guards; the desktop-mode Quick Actions toast keys off `ok`, so a failed CF purge now renders red with the real reason, no JS change needed.

> **Why PATCH:** fix — the `ok` flag stops asserting a success it could not observe and the response gains an additive `cloudflare` field; no settings/schema migration, no removed API.

## [10.2.0] - 2026-07-28

### New

- **`signal-noise/get-machine-readers-summary`** ([inc/abilities-machine-readers.php](inc/abilities-machine-readers.php)): a read-only ability returning the machine-readership summary for a window (1-90 days, default 30) — total reads, top families, declared AI-training reads and their rights-surface slice, plus the sensor version and crawler-list verdict so the numbers can be judged. An unconfigured or unreachable sensor returns `{ok:false, error, days}` with **no** `total` — a zero would tell an agent "no crawler touched this site", which is a different and false claim from "we never asked".
- **A machine-readership sentence for the narrator** ([inc/machine-readers-narration.php](inc/machine-readers-narration.php)): one honest line ("Machine readers read the site N times over the 30-day window; M of those came from declared AI-training families"), silent when there is no data. Crawler reads are never called visits, never called traffic, and never summed with human beacons.
- **Crawler-family delta insight cards** ([inc/machine-readers-insights.php](inc/machine-readers-insights.php)): a family whose reads move materially between comparable windows raises a card. Requires a minimum absolute volume so a 1 → 3 jump does not shout.
- **[docs/MACHINE-READERS.md](docs/MACHINE-READERS.md)**: the surface, the sensor contract (endpoint, auth, both enums), the privacy posture (aggregate-only, fixed enum, raw UA never stored, humans never recorded, never summed with beacons), the deploy and secret requirements, and an end-to-end verification walkthrough.

### Fixed (found by the build's own adversarial review, before merge)

- **`ai_rights` no longer describes a coverage it does not have.** The ability's description named "robots.txt, TDMRep, RSL, llms.txt", but the count only includes the `rights` surface class — `/robots.txt` and `/llms.txt` are their own classes. An agent reading `ai_rights: 0` for a window in which a crawler fetched robots.txt 40 times would have reported "it read none of our declarations". The prose now names exactly what is counted and says explicitly what is excluded; a fixture pins the description against the code.
- **A vacuous test assertion is gone.** The window-clamp pin asserted `strpos( sentence(900), '90' )` — and `"900"` contains `"90"`, so it passed with the clamp deleted (proven by mutation). It now asserts the rendered `90-day` token, negatively asserts `900`, and covers the lower bound. The narrator's honesty vocabulary is now pinned on **both** prose branches, not just one.
- **The payload had been forked in the same file that promised not to fork it.** The ability delegated to the desktop-tile route at 30 days and kept a byte-identical local copy for every other window. There is now ONE builder ([inc/machine-readers-summary.php](inc/machine-readers-summary.php)) that the ability and the tile route both call, and the fixture drives the real builder instead of comparing key lists typed into itself.
- **A family that stops reading is now as reportable as one that starts.** The delta detector iterated the current window only, so a crawler going 900 reads → 0 never carded while a partial fall did. On a surface whose whole point is noticing whether crawlers backed off after we published TDMRep and RSL, the one silence was the flattering direction. It now iterates the union of both windows.
- **The insight module was loaded on every request and called by nothing.** Its cards now render on the Machine Readers tab, from the fetch the tables already made — not a second outbound call, which would have cost a live request on every admin page load while the sensor was down (the read layer caches only success).
- **Two more assertions that proved nothing:** a "payload is never mutated" pin that no implementation could fail (by-value array parameter), replaced with a real one; and a hostile `javascript:` URL row whose `esc_url` stub passed the scheme straight through, so the one sink it claimed to cover was untested.
- **A partially observed prior window can no longer fabricate a trend.** The insight detector only skipped an *entirely* empty window, so a prior window observed on 5 of 30 days (sensor deployed mid-window) rendered "up 500%" from an identical per-day rate. It now requires the prior window to have been observed on at least half the days of the current one, and stays silent otherwise.

> **Why MINOR:** three new user-visible capabilities plus a documented surface; nothing removed or changed. **The unified feed-fetcher column (R4) is NOT in this release** — its build lane died to a transient infrastructure error and was not retried; `rss-feed-tracker` remains the source of truth for feed stats and the Machine Readers tab does not yet mirror them.
